## Motivation Add sglang inference support for **Boogu-Image** ([boogu-project/Boogu-Image](https://github.com/boogu-project/Boogu-Image)). The base model is a 10 B DiT (40 layers = 8 double-stream + 32 single-stream, plus 3 refiner groups), conditioned on Qwen3-VL-8B instruction features, decoded via the FLUX.1-dev `AutoencoderKL`. It ships with a bespoke ascending-time flow-match Euler scheduler that has no direct diffusers equivalent, so this PR wires everything needed to run it end-to-end. Scope of this PR: **base T2I only**. Edit / reference-image, Turbo, and the instruct-reasoner variants are intentionally out of scope and will follow separately. ## Modifications - `runtime/models/dits/boogu_image.py` — DiT: `BooguRMSNormZero` / `BooguLayerNormContinuous`, double-stream + single-stream blocks, 3-axis 3D RoPE (`text / ref-image / noise`) with per-sample windows via `BooguRopeBundle` (msgspec.Struct). Batch is folded into the token dim before rotary so sglang's Triton kernel receives 2D `[num_tokens, head_dim//2]` cos/sin; padded rows use the identity rotation (`cos=1, sin=0`) to match upstream `position_ids=0` semantics. 4D↔5D squeeze at the `ImagePipelineConfig` boundary since Boogu is image-only. - `runtime/models/schedulers/scheduling_boogu_flow_match.py` — flow-match Euler on an **ascending** time axis (`t: 0 → 1`, `prev = sample + (t_next − t) · v`), fundamentally different from `FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler`. Ports the upstream v1 logistic shift (`mu = lin(seq_len)` with `x1=256, y1=0.5, x2=4096, y2=1.15`) and v2 shift (`t / (m − mt + t)` with `m = sqrt(seq_len)/120`). - `configs/pipeline_configs/boogu_image.py` — `BooguImagePipelineConfig`. Chat template routes empty instruction → `SYSTEM_PROMPT_DROP`, non-empty → `SYSTEM_PROMPT_4_T2I` (upstream `system_prompt_follows_task_type=False`, no images). Postprocess reads `.last_hidden_state` (norm-applied); `BooguTextEncodingStage` overrides `_forward_text_encoder` to call `text_encoder.model(...)` because the outer `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration.forward` returns a causal-LM output without `last_hidden_state`. `BooguQwen3VLArchConfig` mirrors the `PretrainedConfig` defaults (`output_attentions=False` etc.) that the HF Qwen3-VL `config.json` doesn't ship. - `runtime/pipelines/boogu_image_pipeline.py` — `_load_config` remaps the on-disk `mllm` / `processor` slots to `text_encoder` / `tokenizer` (via `component_paths` redirect) and relabels the non-diffusers `transformer_boogu` / `scheduling_flow_match_euler_discrete_time_shifting` module strings so the loader library-string assertions pass (`ModelRegistry.resolve_model_cls` keys on the class name). - `configs/models/vaes/boogu_image.py` — subclass of `StableDiffusion3VAEArchConfig` (the SD3 arch config *is* the diffusers `AutoencoderKL`), with FLUX.1-dev's `scaling_factor=0.3611`, `shift_factor=0.1159`. - `configs/models/dits/boogu_image.py`, `configs/sample/boogu_image.py` — DiT and sampling defaults (50 steps, guidance 4.0, 1024²). - `configs/models/fsdp.py`, `registry.py` — `is_boogu_image_layer` FSDP predicate; register `BooguImagePipelineConfig` / `BooguImageSamplingParams` behind a `"boogu-image"` path detector. - `runtime/pipelines_core/stages/text_encoding.py` — **the only shared-path change in this PR.** `align_negative_batch_dim` was applied to both negative embeddings and negative masks, but its 2-D branch is only valid for embeddings: a 2-D *embedding* is `(seq, dim)` with no batch axis, so it must gain one (`unsqueeze(0).repeat(B, 1, 1)` — the Z-Image single-prompt case the branch was written for), whereas a 2-D *mask* is already `(batch, seq)` and must be broadcast in place. Conflating them turned a `[1, S_neg]` mask into `[B, 1, S_neg]`, so any consumer reducing over the sequence dim gets a list of lists instead of one length per request — for Boogu that is an HTTP 500 out of the RoPE builder for every dynamically-batched request (`TypeError: can only concatenate list (not "int") to list`). At batch 1 the broadcast is a no-op (`target_batch == 1` returns the tensor unchanged), which is why the one-shot `generate` path never surfaced it. The helper now takes a kw-only `batchless_2d` flag; both mask call sites pass `batchless_2d=False`. - `runtime/models/dits/boogu_image.py` — `@torch.compiler.disable` on `BooguRopeEmbedder.forward`, which is what makes `--enable-torch-compile` usable for this model. Dynamo's polyfill calls `cls.__new__(cls, *args)` and msgspec's C-level `__new__` rejects it, so compiling the DiT raised from the RoPE embedder's `BooguRopeBundle` return value. Position ids depend only on sequence lengths and image sizes, never on the latents, and the call is ~0.5 ms, so keeping it out of the graph costs nothing and lets the remaining 40 layers compile. - `test/unit/test_text_encoding_negative_batch.py` — new. A shared `[1, seq]` negative mask stays 2-D when broadcast to a batch (and still reduces to one length per request); a 2-D `(seq, dim)` embedding still gains a batch axis; batch 1 is unchanged. Follows [`no-getattr-defensive`](.claude/rules/no-getattr-defensive.md), [`no-dataclasses`](.claude/rules/no-dataclasses.md) (new containers are `msgspec.Struct`; config classes are grandfathered `@dataclass`), [`general-code-style`](.claude/rules/general-code-style.md). ## Accuracy Tests - Scheduler: bit-identical to upstream across `static-v1` / `dynamic-v1` / `dynamic-v2` / `do_shift=False` × steps ∈ {50, 40, 28}, and `step()` integration over 40 steps (max delta `0.0`). - Weight loading: 942 checkpoint keys → 888 model params, 0 missing / 0 unexpected / 0 shape mismatch. - Single-GPU T2I end-to-end (1024×1024, guidance 4.0, seed 0): output image aligns with the reference `inference_simple.py` prompt (elderly scavenger + trash can + red traffic light + Leica street-photography aesthetic). - Unit tests: `pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_text_encoding_negative_batch.py -q` → **3 passed**. Shared negative-conditioning / CFG paths re-run to confirm no other model regressed (`test_text_encoding_cache.py`, `test_cfg_gating.py`, `test_sampling_params.py`, plus the new file) → **36 passed, 8 subtests passed**. - Server end-to-end: the benchmark below produced 10 images (1 warmup + 3 sequential + 2 concurrent + 4 concurrent) with zero exceptions in the server log, at scheduler-reported batch sizes 1 / 2 / 4. - The `text_encoding.py` fix is shape-only and a no-op at batch 1, so single-request output is unchanged by construction; the batched shapes are locked by the new unit tests. `@torch.compiler.disable` keeps the RoPE builder in eager rather than altering it, so it does not move numerics either. - 50-step parity vs the upstream diffusers reference (same `seed=42`, cyberpunk prompt / gallery row 1): injecting byte-identical initial noise **and** conditioning into both stacks leaves the initial latent bit-identical (max abs diff `0.0`) and the step-1 latent within **0.53%** rel-L2 (cosine `0.99997`) — a single denoise step is numerically equivalent across backends. Over 50 CFG steps at guidance 4.0 this compounds to step-50 latent rel-L2 ≈ 72% and final-image PSNR 12.3 dB / SSIM 0.40 (see the Qualitative Comparison section), i.e. benign last-bit bf16 kernel drift (FlashInfer/fused vs SDPA), not a structural difference. ## Qualitative Comparison (upstream diffusers vs sglang native) Same weights, `seed=42`, 1024×1024, 50 steps, `guidance_scale=4.0`. Images are width-limited to 320px; click any cell to view full 1024×1024. | Prompt | diffusers (upstream) | sglang (native) | |---|---|---| | A futuristic cyberpunk city at night, neon reflections on wet streets | | | | A cute orange tabby kitten sitting in a field of sunflowers, golden hour lighting, photorealistic | | | | A serene Japanese garden with a red maple tree, koi pond and stone lantern in autumn | | | | A steaming bowl of ramen with a soft-boiled egg and chopsticks, close-up food photography | | | | An astronaut riding a horse on Mars, dramatic cinematic lighting | | |
Parity note (same-seed divergence is expected, not a bug) Feeding byte-identical initial noise **and** identical conditioning embeddings into both stacks: step-1 latent rel-L2 = 0.53% (cosine 0.99997), step-50 = 72%, final image PSNR 12.3 dB / SSIM 0.40. A single denoise step is numerically equivalent between the two backends; the divergence is compounding bf16 kernel drift amplified over 50 CFG steps at guidance 4.0 — a different-but-valid sample from the same distribution, not a structural difference.
## Speed Tests and Profiling H20 (95.6 GiB), bf16, `Boogu-Image-0.1-Base` (10.29B DiT, 40 layers), `guidance_scale=4.0`, `seed=42`, fixed prompt set. Sections 1–3 are 1024²/50 steps with the upstream diffusers pipeline as reference (identical weights, sglang on GPU 2, diffusers on GPU 0); section 4 uses vllm-omni's published 512²/28-step config. The native-backend gate was verified on every sglang run (no `diffusers backend` / `Loaded diffusers pipeline` in any log). Shared env: `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`.
Commands sglang one-shot and server. `serve` opens its HTTP port *before* warmup runs (`/health` answers 200 while the GPU is still warming), so readiness is gated on the `fired up and ready to roll` log line: ```bash python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.entrypoints.cli.main generate \ --backend=sglang --model-path $MODEL --prompt "$PROMPT" \ --width 1024 --height 1024 --num-inference-steps 50 --guidance-scale 4.0 \ --seed 42 --save-output --warmup --dit-cpu-offload false \ --perf-dump-path outputs/diffusion_benchmarks/$LABEL.json \ [--enable-torch-compile] [--enable-cfg-parallel] python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.entrypoints.cli.main serve \ --model-path $MODEL --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31000 \ --batching-max-size 4 --batching-delay-ms 100 \ --enable-batching-metrics --dit-cpu-offload false curl -x '' -s http://127.0.0.1:31000/v1/images/generations \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"prompt":"'"$PROMPT"'","width":1024,"height":1024, "num_inference_steps":50,"guidance_scale":4.0,"seed":42,"n":1}' ``` Upstream diffusers reference. `device=cuda:0` must be exported *before* importing `boogu` — it gates upstream's own fused RMSNorm and fused SwiGLU, so leaving it unset understates the reference. One 50-step warmup pass is discarded: ```python import os; os.environ["device"] = "cuda:0" # before the boogu import import torch from boogu.pipelines.boogu.pipeline_boogu import BooguImagePipeline pipe = BooguImagePipeline.from_pretrained(MODEL, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, trust_remote_code=True).to("cuda:0") # str -> batch 1; list -> batch_size = len(list) (pipeline_boogu.py:2743) pipe(instruction=PROMPT, negative_instruction="", height=1024, width=1024, max_input_image_pixels=1024 * 1024, max_input_image_side_length=2048, num_inference_steps=50, text_guidance_scale=4.0, generator=torch.Generator("cuda:0").manual_seed(42)) ``` Section 4, sglang side — the in-tree benchmark client, one server lifetime per config. With `--enable-torch-compile` *and* `--batching-max-size > 1` the sweep runs twice and only the second, compile-warm pass is reported; see the section 4 caveats for why `--warmup-requests` cannot cover it: ```bash python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.entrypoints.cli.main serve \ --model-path $MODEL --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31011 \ --batching-max-size {1,4} --batching-delay-ms 100 \ --enable-batching-metrics --dit-cpu-offload false --enable-torch-compile true for conc in 1 2 4; do python python/sglang/multimodal_gen/benchmarks/bench_serving.py \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31011 --dataset random --task text-to-image \ --width 512 --height 512 --num-inference-steps 28 \ --num-prompts 10 --max-concurrency $conc --warmup-requests 4 \ --disable-tqdm --output-file c$conc.json done ``` vllm-omni side (their own harness and config, model repointed at our local checkpoint, baseline assertion replaced by `skip-performance-assertion`): ```bash python -m pytest tests/dfx/perf/scripts/run_diffusion_benchmark.py \ --test-config-file tests/dfx/perf/tests/test_boogu_image_h20_local.json -s -v ```
### 1. Optimization stack vs upstream diffusers, one-shot latency The diffusers reference is repeated per row so each sglang config is compared to the closest diffusers configuration — 68.65 s eager (its own fused RMSNorm / SwiGLU / FA on) for the non-compile rows, 66.51 s (+ `torch.compile`) for the compile rows. Head-dim padding and CFG parallel have no equivalent there. | config | diffusers (upstream) | sglang (native) | sglang speedup | sglang vs diffusers | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | eager, 1 GPU | 68.65 | 69.49 | 1.00× | 0.99× | | + `--enable-torch-compile` | 66.51 | 59.87 | **1.16×** | **1.11×** | | + head-dim padded to FA bucket, eager | 68.65 | 64.67 | **1.07×** | **1.06×** | | + head-dim padded + `--enable-torch-compile` | 66.51 | **54.54** | **1.27×** | **1.22×** | | + `--enable-cfg-parallel`, 2 GPU | 68.65 | 34.79 | **2.00×** | **1.97×** | | + CFG parallel ×2 + compile | 66.51 | **29.93** | **2.32×** | **2.22×** | - Eager baselines agree within 1.2%, so the ports are at parity before any lever. - `torch.compile` buys diffusers only 3.1% (68.65 → 66.51, fast paths already on) but 1.16× here — and is reachable only via the `@torch.compiler.disable` change in this PR. Compile × CFG-parallel stacks cleanly: 2.01 × 1.16 = 2.33 predicted vs 2.336× measured. - Best single-GPU 54.54 s is **1.22×** diffusers' own best; CFG-parallel ×2 + compile 29.93 s is **2.22×**. - Head-dim padding routes Boogu's head_dim=120 through FlashAttention by zero-padding Q/K/V to 128 (softmax_scale pinned to 1/√120) and slicing back — the trick `sana_wm_components._sana_wm_sdpa` already uses for head_dim=112. Kernel test matches SDPA within bf16 noise (rel-L2 = 3.9 × 10⁻⁵). The two padding rows were re-measured as a four-cell A/B on one commit, the only variable being `_padded_head_dim` (128 vs `self.head_dim`, which makes the selector reject FA at head size 120 and fall back to `torch_sdpa` — confirmed per cell from the `Attention backends for transformer` log line); all four cells reproduce the table within 0.21%. The gain is resolution-dependent: attention is 22.5% of DiT GPU time at 1024²'s 4352 joint tokens but roughly a third of that at 512²'s 1280, since attention FLOPs grow as S² and the linear layers as S, so the same A/B at 512² returns only +0.27% (section 4). ### 2. Server mode with dynamic batching Warmup is `server warmup req (1024x1024, 2/50 steps)` = 6.12 s, then `fired up and ready to roll` — 210 s from launch. Batch sizes are the scheduler's own `Dynamic batch dispatch` metric, not the request count. Compile rows are compile-warm (first request at a new batch dim recompiles: 315 s at batch 2). SDPA eager (= section 1's `eager, 1 GPU`): | concurrency | scheduler dispatch | per-request latency (s) | wall (s) | img/s | vs 1 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | `size=1/4 delay` | 70.48 / 70.00 / 70.77 → median **70.48** | 70.48 | 0.0142 | 1.000× | | 2 | `size=2/4 delay` | 137.01 / 137.01 | 137.02 | 0.0146 | 1.03× | | 4 | `size=4/4 config_cap:4` | 271.18 ×4 | 271.19 | 0.0148 | 1.04× | Padded FA + `--enable-torch-compile` (= section 1's best single-GPU row): | concurrency | scheduler dispatch | per-request latency (s) | wall (s) | img/s | vs 1 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | `size=1/4 delay` | 55.44 / 55.15 / 55.15 → median **55.15** | 55.44 | 0.0181 | 1.000× | | 2 | `size=2/4 delay` | 110.51 / 110.51 | 110.52 | 0.0181 | 1.00× | | 4 | `size=4/4 config_cap:4` | 218.16 ×4 | 218.17 | 0.0183 | 1.01× | Serving overhead is small — 70.48 s through HTTP + ZMQ + scheduler vs 69.49 s one-shot, **+1.4%**. Padded FA + compile is **1.28× / 1.24× / 1.24×** faster per request at concurrency 1 / 2 / 4, matching section 1's 1.27×. ### 3. Batching headroom at this resolution, vs diffusers | batch | diffusers ms/forward | diffusers img/s | vs 1 | sglang (SDPA) img/s | vs 1 | sglang (padded FA + compile) img/s | vs 1 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 683.3 | 0.0146 | 1.000× | 0.0142 | 1.000× | 0.0181 | 1.000× | | 2 | 1331.9 (1.95×) | 0.0150 | 1.027× | 0.0146 | 1.03× | 0.0181 | 1.00× | | 4 | 2617.5 (3.83×) | 0.0152 | 1.046× | 0.0148 | 1.04× | 0.0183 | 1.01× | diffusers' per-forward scales 1.00 / 1.95 / 3.83 — essentially linear — so one 1024² image (4096 image + 256 instruction = 4352 joint tokens) already saturates the H20 and batching is worth ~1–4% for any implementation. All three curves agreeing on the flat shape is the result: this PR makes batching *correct*, and section 1's multi-GPU path is where throughput comes from. Peak memory, per engine: sglang 29 950 / 34 558 / 44 794 MB (server's own `Peak memory usage`), diffusers 36.91 / 38.54 / 42.54 GiB (`torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated`). ### 4. Cross-engine check against vllm-omni, on the same GPU vllm-omni [PR #4995](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/4995) ports the same model, but on different hardware, so its published numbers support no claim about either implementation. Their stack was installed (own uv venv, `vllm 0.26.0` + vllm-omni at upstream main `67c54777`, torch 2.11.0+cu130) and **their harness and their published config were run on the same H20, GPU 1** — the card our own sweep used. That config is `tests/dfx/perf/tests/test_boogu_image_vllm_omni.json` (512×512, 28 steps, 10 prompts, `max-concurrency` 1/2/4, 4 warmup requests at concurrency 4, negative prompt on, guidance 4.0 with CFG on), **not** the 1024² command in their PR body. Their pipeline profiler costs 0.5–1.0%, so their profiler-off numbers are quoted. 30/30 requests succeeded per run. Medians are used throughout: at 10 prompts / concurrency 4 the run is only 2.5 waves, so the partly-empty first wave biases every mean, while medians match Little's Law within 0.15%. Each engine at its own best. Both harnesses share a client lineage and emit the same fields (`throughput_qps`, `latency_median`), so the rows line up directly: latency is the median of 10 requests at concurrency 1, throughput the best over concurrency 1 / 2 / 4. | engine | best config | per-image latency (s) | throughput (img/s) | |---|---|---:|---:| | vllm-omni | compile on by default; request batching unavailable | 8.502 | 0.1192 | | sglang (this PR) | padded FA + `--enable-torch-compile` | **8.259** | **0.1341** | | ratio (sglang / vllm-omni) | | **1.029×** | **1.125×** | The two sglang figures come from different `--batching-max-size` values — 8.259 s at `maxb 1`, 0.1341 img/s at `maxb 4` — because batching trades 0.115 s of single-image latency (the `--batching-delay-ms 100` window, with nothing to merge at concurrency 1) for +10.7% throughput at concurrency 4. Run `maxb 4` when loaded, `maxb 1` when latency-bound. - **They compile the DiT by default** (`Regional compilation applied to 42 module(s) for repeated blocks [...]`, no flag); our defaults are eager and `batching_max_size = 1` (`server_args.py:355`). Default vs default **we lose 11.6%**, and only this PR unblocks the flip — worth 1.16× here, the same as section 1's 1024² figure. Compile vs compile with batching off the two engines are within 1.6%: the denoising loops are at parity, and the gap above comes from the levers around them. - **Their concurrency curve is flat for a structural reason, not a batching result.** `pipeline_boogu_image.py:201` sets `supports_request_batch = False`; `diffusion_engine.py:205` raises `ValueError` for any `max_num_seqs > 1`; the alternative `--step-execution` path needs `prepare_encode()` / `denoise_step()` / `step_scheduler()` / `post_decode()`, none of which their pipeline implements. Their log confirms `max_num_seqs=1 max_wait_ms=0.0`, `batch_size=1`. Per-pipeline gap, not an engine limit: `qwen_image`, `sd3`, `flux`, `ltx2` all set `supports_request_batch = True`. - **Head-dim padding is nearly free at this resolution** — +0.27% against +7.5% / +9.7% at 1024² in section 1. A 1280-token joint sequence spends far less of its time in attention than a 4352-token one. | lever | sglang (this PR) | vllm-omni Boogu | upstream diffusers | |---|---|---|---| | `torch.compile` on the DiT | 1.16× at both resolutions, unblocked here | on by default | 1.03× | | request batching | +10.7% qps at concurrency 4 | unavailable | +4.6% at batch 4 | | CFG parallel, 2 GPU | **2.00×** | unavailable | unavailable | | stacked | **2.32×** | — | — | Caveats: single run per point. For the `maxb 4` figure the sweep was run twice against one server and the second, compile-warm pass reported — with `--enable-torch-compile` the first request at a previously unseen batch dim recompiles inside the measured window, so cold pass 1 at concurrency 2 reads qps 0.0560 with p99 116.4 s against a 15.51 s median. Their harness posts t2i to `/v1/chat/completions` while `bench_serving.py` posts `/v1/images/generations` (each engine's documented path). All four GPUs carried an external tenant at ~80% utilization throughout, applying to both engines equally — the point of measuring on one box. ## Follow-up work (not in this PR) Called out so reviewers know the current boundary; these will land separately: - **Sequence parallelism (Ulysses/SP).** `--ulysses-degree 2` does not yet work for this model — the latent `rearrange` is over 5 dims and the 7 KV heads do not divide by the SP degree, so it needs a `shard_latents_for_sp` override in `base.py` and a fix to the head-count assert at `usp.py:263`. CFG parallelism in section 1 is unaffected and is the multi-GPU path that works today. - **Cache-DiT (step-layer caching, ~1.5–2× lossy).** Boogu is not yet registered in `_CUSTOM_BLOCK_ADAPTER_SPECS`; the adapter carries a single block-list attribute while Boogu has two (`double_stream_layers` = 8, `single_stream_layers` = 32), so registration has to handle both. Gated on a PSNR/SSIM check since it is lossy. - **Warm up serving benchmarks at the real step count.** `bench_serving.py:591` pins warmup requests to `num_inference_steps=1` because the server overrides them anyway (`warmup_request_builder.py:394` → `Req.set_as_warmup`), and issues them serially — so warmup pre-warms neither the real denoise shape nor a batch dim, and under `--enable-torch-compile` with `--batching-max-size > 1` the first request at each new batch dim recompiles inside the measured window. vllm-omni's harness avoids this by warming at `warmup-num-inference-steps=28, warmup-concurrency=4`. Section 4 works around it by reporting the second of two passes; the fix is to let warmup requests carry the benchmark's step count and concurrency. - **I2I / edit and reference-image** (and Turbo / instruct-reasoner), per the scope note in Motivation. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #30752695530](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30752695530) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #30752695446](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30752695446) --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #35293327136](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35293327136) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #35293327111](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35293327111) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #35293327160](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35293327160)

issues.title: [DeepSeek V4.1] Add DeepSelect JIT kernel.
issues.body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

#39421.

This PR moves DeepSelect to the existing JIT infrastructure so only the required call signature is compiled for the local CUDA target.

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

- Remove the DeepSelect AOT target, bindings, and explicit instantiations.
- Move the vendored kernel headers under `jit/csrc/deepselect/vendor`.
- Add a JIT C++ entry point and Python wrapper for BF16/FP32, int32/int64
  indices, normal and cluster kernels, sorting, offsets, and variable lengths.
- Keep the DeepSelect CUDA algorithm unchanged. The three kernel headers only
  drop includes of the deleted AOT `topk_select.h` files.
- Add C++ argument/storage validation, aligned output staging, and empty-batch
  handling.
- Use the JIT framework's local target directly. No `ScopedCudaDevice`, runtime
  C++ SM check, or `override_jit_cuda_arch` is added.

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling


The complete candidate path was benchmarked on NVIDIA H20 using:

- FP32 candidate logits.
- `topk_blocks=2048`.
- 20 warmup iterations.
- 100 measured iterations.
- Median latency.
- L2 cache flushing before every measured iteration.
- Two complete benchmark runs; the tables report the mean of the two medians.

```text
candidate block-score reduction
  -> candidate Top-K

  -> downstream paged Top-K
```

issues.title: Add triton autotune on the Mamba2 SSD kernels
issues.body: ## Motivation The Mamba2 SSD Triton kernels were adapted from vLLM without their `@triton.autotune` decorators: sglang's original import (#10988) carried them commented out, and #10909 deleted the commented blocks while re-syncing the ops. The launchers still size their grids from `META["BLOCK_SIZE_*"]`, so every kernel silently ran at its signature default of `BLOCK_SIZE_* = 16` -- a 10x+ loss on the prefill kernels. Upstream vLLM has these decorators live today. ## Modifications - Restore `@triton.autotune` on `ssd_bmm`, `ssd_chunk_scan`, `ssd_chunk_state` and `ssd_state_passing`. The config lists and keys are verbatim from current `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/`, so these blocks stay diffable on the next upstream sync. - `_chunk_state_varlen_kernel` is sglang-only -- vLLM replaced it with `gather_initial_states.py` driven by `cu_chunk_seqlens` -- so it reuses the `_chunk_state_fwd_kernel` list (same tile-shape family). - Add `**autotune_cache_kwargs` (the existing sglang FLA idiom, `kernels/ops/attention/fla/utils.py`) so a tuning result survives process restarts instead of being re-measured on every server launch. - Add `prune_configs_by` / `prune_oversized_tiles`, which caps each `BLOCK_SIZE_*` at `next_power_of_2` of the dimension it tiles. A tile wider than its dimension computes a fully masked remainder over the same grid, so it is dominated. This is the fix for the `test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` CI timeout -- see below. - Fix `bench_one_batch` on Mamba models: `selective_state_update` dispatches through a process-global backend that only the Scheduler installs, so every Mamba model died during decode CUDA-graph capture inside `load_model`. It is now initialized from a helper shared by `latency_test` and `correctness_test`, so `--correctness-test` is covered too. ## CI cost The 30-minute timeout on the previous run was real and caused by this PR. Autotuning is per distinct key, and `test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` spans many: `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel` alone sees ~22 keys over the CI-reduced matrix (Triton folds the tensor dtypes into the key on top of `chunk_size`/`hdim`/`dstate`), at 23 configs each -- ~500 compile+bench cycles for one kernel, and ~4x that across all six. A persistent cache does not help here, since the cold pytest process never gets a hit. The prune collapses the small CI shapes to a handful of configs each (`hdim=5, dstate=5, chunk_size=16` -> 1 config; `hdim=32, dstate=32, chunk_size=8` -> 1), without touching the test matrix. ## Accuracy Tests Autotuning selects `BLOCK_SIZE_K`, which sets the K-split of the fp32 `tl.dot` accumulation, so output is **not** bit-identical to the `BLOCK_SIZE_* = 16` defaults. `lm_eval` GSM8K (5-shot), Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4, TP4: | | main | + autotune | | --- | ---: | ---: | | flexible-extract | 0.9401 ± 0.0065 | 0.9409 ± 0.0065 | | strict-match | 0.9378 ± 0.0067 | 0.9393 ± 0.0066 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling **End-to-end serving**, Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4 on GB300 TP4, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024: | Concurrency | Total tok/s (main) | Total tok/s (+autotune) | Speedup | tok/s/user (main) | tok/s/user (+autotune) | Speedup | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 16 | 10,981 | 13,264 | **1.21x** | 104.9 | 110.2 | **1.05x** | | 32 | 15,728 | 17,751 | **1.13x** | 78.0 | 85.4 | **1.10x** | | 64 | 20,772 | 23,662 | **1.14x** | 53.0 | 59.5 | **1.12x** | | 128 | 24,877 | 29,892 | **1.20x** | 33.9 | 39.0 | **1.15x** | | 256 | 28,190 | 35,747 | **1.27x** | 20.0 | 24.3 | **1.22x** | | 512 | 29,558 | 37,776 | **1.28x** | 16.8 | 20.5 | **1.22x** | ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - issues.title: [Cleanup] Deduplicate kernel tests, diffusion fixtures and benchmark helpers
issues.body:
## Motivation

Kernel and diffusion tests repeat input/reference code, fixture setup and whole test bodies. Some benchmarks also carry copied or unused helpers and stale import paths. This cleanup removes 1,426 net lines across 26 files while retaining the numerical checks, backend-specific dispatch, input matrices and CI registrations.

## Modifications

- Share paged-MQA fixtures, PyTorch reference and comparison logic between CuTe DSL and DeepGEMM tests; retain both complete backend matrices. Share the original AWQ input packer between dense and MoE repack tests.
- Parameterize metadata-copy small/large batches into one body per backend. Keep all 40 numerical cases and both dtype rejection tests. Delete unreachable reference branches and single-shot performance-print scaffolding from correctness tests.
- Consolidate diffusion gate/capture/fallback cases, FP32 LayerNorm cache checks and VAE defaults. Fold upsampler call counts into numerical tests and replace the copied full-model reference with an unfused GroupNorm + activation override; keep the independent ResBlock oracle and original CPU/GPU case boundaries. Reuse the existing parent server-args fixture in three SANA-WM suites.
- Share DeepSeek-V3 benchmark shape tables and FP8 input preparation; fix grouped-GEMM helper imports and use DeepGEMM's current testing-module import for `calc_diff`. Preserve the original unrounded FP32 scales rather than substituting the production UE8M0 quantizer.
- Delete the copied DeepEP benchmark utility file and reuse existing test helpers; keep its CLI-specific distributed initializer unchanged. Remove unused FA4 backward/profiling helpers, an uncalled vLLM GEMM wrapper/import and three uncalled MMMU data helpers.

## Accuracy Tests

Rebased onto main `d507accadc` and validated on GB300 (SM103), PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130:

| Existing tests | Result |
| --- | --- |
| CuTe DSL + DeepGEMM paged MQA, full matrices | 384 passed |
| Diffusion fusion, norm/cache, fallback and VAE loader | 69 passed, 8 subtests passed |
| Residual gate | 35 passed |
| Metadata copy + AWQ repack | 58 passed, 30 skipped |
| SANA-WM streaming/realtime suites | 23 passed |

Total: **569 passed, 30 skipped, 8 subtests passed**. The 30 skips are JIT-vs-AOT comparisons because this environment does not expose the old AOT repack operators; the independent JIT numerical checks ran. Metadata/AWQ and SANA-WM results match the before-cleanup run on the same base. Original first-pass diffusion cases also passed before consolidation. No numerical tolerance was relaxed.

Additional validation:

- 88 old/new FP8 payload-and-scale comparisons (CPU/CUDA, BF16/FP32, zero and padded inputs), 24 exact AWQ packer comparisons and all four original shape tables at TP 1/2/4/8/16 match.
- The generated metadata-copy parameter matrix is identical; all 11 CI registration calls are unchanged. Retained MMMU functions are AST-identical, with four prompt-construction smoke checks.
- All four affected DeepSeek/block-wise benchmark CLIs pass `--help` import smoke checks. Shared MQA and moved/reused DeepEP helpers retain their original implementations. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No inference behavior changes or inference speedup claim. The only runtime-file edit is a formatting-only change in `logits_processor.py` required by the repository-wide Ruff check (AST unchanged). DeepEP helpers pass 18 exact tensor/scalar comparisons and CUDA-event timer smoke checks; the retained FA4 forward timer passes with AMP off/on. Benchmark providers and timed callbacks are unchanged. Full multi-node DeepEP and GEMM tuning sweeps were not run.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Run the affected existing tests; no new test suite added.
- [x] Review numerical coverage, backend guards and CI registrations.
- [x] Document validation and its scope above.

issues.title: [Diffusion][Docs] Add single-GPU large-VRAM performance notes (B300)
issues.body:
## Summary

Profile-driven measurements on a **single B300 (275 GB, SM103)** across nine single-GPU-runnable diffusion models (following the `sglang-diffusion-benchmark-profile` skill: fixed seed/prompt/shape, perf dumps + `torch.profiler`, byte-identical / SSIM-PSNR correctness gates).

This documents two findings that change which flags are actually fastest on a large-VRAM single GPU, and fixes two recipe rows.

## Findings

1. **Launch-bound small models gain the most from BCG**
   - SANA1.5-1.6B (image): denoise **0.70s → 0.23s (-67%)**, bit-identical.
   - SANA-Video (832x480, 17 frames): **1.24s → 0.96s (-22%)**, bit-identical.
   - Compute-bound models (LongCat-Image, Qwen-Image, Z-Image, Cosmos3-Edge, FLUX.1-dev, Wan2.1-1.3B) show **no** BCG or `torch.compile` gain — profiles show GEMM + flash-attention + already-fused norm/GELU saturating the device.

2. **Component CPU offload is a pessimization on a 275 GB card**
   - Presets enable `--text-encoder-cpu-offload` for memory-bound cards, but the whole model stays resident, so the H2D/D2H round trip is pure overhead. Dropping it on LingBot-Video-MoE was **8% faster end to end** (3.80s → 3.49s, bit-identical).

## Recipe fixes
- **SANA-Video**: the BCG recipe now includes `--warmup-num-frames 17`. Without it, warmup captures the 81-frame sampling default and a 17-frame request misses the captured graph → falls back to eager, measured **slower than baseline** (1.40s vs 1.24s).
- **LingBot Video MoE**: note that `--text-encoder-cpu-offload` should be dropped on large-VRAM single GPUs.

Docs-only change.

issues.title: [MLX] Upgrade to Torch 2.13/MLX 0.32+ and redesign the Torch-MLX tensor bridge
issues.body:
## Motivation

MLX 0.32 can import Torch MPS allocations directly, while Torch 2.13 changes
the runtime and DLPack edge cases that the Apple Silicon integration must
support. The existing bridge stages MPS tensors through CPU memory, obscures
borrowed-versus-owned lifetimes, and pays payload-sized copies. Separately,
diffusion's `SGLANG_USE_MLX` norm override is not selected by normal MPS
`CustomOp` dispatch; forcing those norms through Torch-MLX crossings is slower
end to end.

This PR upgrades the `srt_mps` runtime, fails fast on unsupported Torch/MLX
pairs, separates owned copies from scoped zero-copy borrows, and removes the
unreachable diffusion-only MLX fallback. It does not replace the existing SRT
MLX runner; the stacked
[yeahdongcn/sglang#7](https://github.com/yeahdongcn/sglang/pull/7) consumes these
bridge primitives while redesigning that backend.

## Modifications

- Update `srt_mps` in `python/pyproject_other.toml` to Torch 2.13.0, MLX >=
  0.32.0, TorchVision 0.28.0, TorchAudio 2.11.0, and TorchCodec 0.15.0.
  The versions stay directly in `srt_mps`, matching the existing extra layout;
  `all_mps` inherits them through `srt_mps`. MLX keeps a 0.32.0 minimum but
  has no upper bound; startup accepts newer stable MLX releases. TorchAudio
  2.11 remains intentional and was validated with the tested Torch 2.13 MPS
  stack. CPU and standalone `diffusion_mps` dependency lists are unchanged.
- Move the SRT MLX version/device validation to the earliest model-independent
  `ServerArgs` bootstrap. With `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1`, SGLang requires stable
  Torch 2.13.x and stable MLX >= 0.32.0. Older MLX, Torch outside 2.13.x, and
  rc/dev builds fail before model path resolution/downloads and before the
  dummy-model short circuit. With the flag unset, importing SGLang still does
  not import MLX.
- Redesign `tensor_bridge.py` around explicit ownership and batching:
  - `torch_to_mlx` creates and materializes MLX-owned storage when the result
    must outlive its Torch source.
  - `MlxTensorView` and `borrow_torch_tensors` provide persistent and batched
    zero-copy MPS borrows while retaining every Torch storage owner.
  - `mlx_call` and `mlx_call_multi` validate the target before work, fence
    Torch producers once, keep all borrowed inputs alive through lazy
    evaluation, evaluate ordinary multi-output results at one shared `mx.eval`
    boundary, batch the additional materialization boundary required by
    negative-stride outputs, and export them through DLPack.
  - `mlx_to_torch` uses evaluated DLPack views for MPS and explicit CPU views.
    Positive-stride layouts, including CPU float64, remain zero-copy.
    Negative-stride MLX views are materialized because Torch 2.13's DLPack
    importer otherwise aborts the process instead of raising a Python
    exception; unsupported CPU dtypes fail instead of silently narrowing.
  This PR intentionally owns these shared Torch-MLX bridge primitives. The
  stacked MPS redesign in
  [yeahdongcn/sglang#7](https://github.com/yeahdongcn/sglang/pull/7) consumes
  them for Torch-owned model weights and provider outputs, while its
  provider-specific invalidation callbacks and phase timing stay in that PR.
- Remove `mps_fallback.py`, route diffusion MPS kernels to native Torch
  fallbacks, and use `F.layer_norm`/`F.rms_norm` instead of the old manual
  decomposition. The shared fallback remains compatible with both the
  default Torch 2.11 and CPU-backend Torch 2.12 stacks. RMSNorm preserves the
  optional-bias and input-dtype contracts even with fp32 parameters. The
  removed rotary and scale/shift entries were
  already aliases to Torch implementations; only the norm entries had
  MLX-specific implementations.
- Remove diffusion's `SGLANG_USE_MLX` runtime handling and clarify in the
  existing documentation that the variable applies only to SRT serving. SRT
  keeps its existing `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1` opt-in.
- Add Torch 2.13-compatible Triton import-stub symbols used by Inductor on
  MPS.
- Rebase the branch onto upstream `main` at `978244d67148`; update VAE and
  Transformer component loaders to the upstream unified residency API so MPS
  layerwise offload remains valid after the upstream loader refactor.

The diffusion MLX norm path is intentionally dropped after tracing and
measurement. `CustomOp.dispatch_forward()` routes MPS to `forward_native`, so
the legacy MLX override is unreachable in the normal production graph. Sana
instrumentation confirmed zero legacy entrypoint calls, and forcing all 58
norms per DiT forward through MLX was slower end to end. Isolated large fp32
LayerNorm microbenchmarks sometimes favored MLX by a few percent, but the result was not
robust across the common fp16/bf16 cases and did not justify repeated
framework crossings. A future fully MLX-resident diffusion path can be
evaluated separately.

## Accuracy Tests

- `PATH="$PWD/sglang-metal/bin:$PATH" SGLANG_USE_MLX=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 ./sglang-metal/bin/python test/run_suite.py --hw mlx --suite stage-a-unit-test-mlx`
  - **21/21 registered test files passed locally** on Apple M1 at PR head
    `c1f34a81d1`, including bridge, startup runtime gate, Triton-stub, and
    diffusion fallback coverage.
  - The focused bridge/runtime/diffusion-loader bundle passed **121 tests plus 36 subtests** after the rebase.
- All four new test files are registered in `stage-a-unit-test-mlx`.
  `test_diffusion_torch_fallback.py` is additionally registered in
  `base-a-test-cpu`, `base-b-test-cpu`, and `base-b-test-cpu-arm64`.
- The same six fallback UTs passed **6/6** in isolated Torch 2.11.0 and 2.12.0
  CPU environments, including fp16/bf16 inputs with fp32 parameters.
- Runtime tests verify Torch 2.12/2.14, MLX 0.31, and Torch/MLX rc/dev builds
  are rejected, while stable Torch 2.13 patch releases and stable MLX releases
  from 0.32.0 onward (including future minor versions) are accepted.
  Incompatible versions abort `ServerArgs` creation even for
  `model_path="dummy"`; missing MLX, unavailable PyTorch MPS, and unavailable
  MLX Metal each produce actionable startup errors. The disabled path
  constructs `ServerArgs` without importing MLX.
- Bridge ownership checks cover owned/scoped/persistent lifetimes, source
  mutation and deletion, single-fence batched borrows, shared-eval multi-output
  calls, bfloat16/non-contiguous views, CPU float64 and unsupported dtypes,
  autograd detachment, invalid-target fail-fast behavior, and negative-stride
  materialization in an abort-safe subprocess.
- SRT serving smoke with local `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`: both
  `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1` and the no-env Torch-MPS path returned **200** from
  `/health` and `/generate`. For prompt `The capital of France is` with
  greedy 8-token decoding, both paths returned identical output token IDs
  `[12095, 13, 576, 6722, 315, 9625, 374, 1083]` and text
  `Paris. The capital of France is also`.
- Sana 600M, prompt `A small red cube on a plain white background`, seed 42,
  256x256, 4 steps: native Torch output and the hypothetical all-MLX norm
  output remained visually consistent (PSNR 41.95 dB; max pixel delta 50).
  The final `mlx_call` image was byte-identical to the earlier explicit-
  keepalive MLX image.
  The ordinary Sana path recorded 58 Torch norm calls per DiT forward and zero
  legacy norm-fallback entrypoint calls. After the rebase, a native Torch-MPS
  Sana smoke with the same 256x256/4-step configuration produced a valid RGB
  PNG in 24.87s with 6.33GB peak memory.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Environment: Apple M1, macOS 26.5.2, Torch 2.13.0, MLX 0.32.0. All timings
include the required producer/consumer synchronization. The operation table
reports end-to-end norm-call timings, including bridge/export and
synchronization, rather than raw kernel-only timings. It is one representative
median-after-warmup run; an independent rerun preserved the common-Sana
ordering but flipped whether large-fp32 MLX was slightly ahead or behind.

| Case | Torch native | MLX owned copy | MLX scoped borrow |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Sana RMSNorm `(1,300,1152)` fp32 | 230 us | 676 us | 259 us |
| Sana LayerNorm `(1,256,1152)` bf16 | 254 us | 913 us | 324 us |
| Flux LayerNorm `(1,4096,3072)` fp32 | 2508 us | 4763 us | 2441 us |

Bridge A/B directly calls the final `mlx_call(lambda a: a, tensor)` API
against the pre-change CPU-staging implementation at the branch merge base
(Apple M1, Torch 2.13.0, MLX 0.32.0). The table reports the range of per-batch
p50 values across three independent batches; each batch used 5 warmups and 20
measured samples with producer/consumer synchronization:

| Logical tensor | dtype / payload | Old CPU-staging p50 range | Final `mlx_call` p50 range | Minimum paired speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `(4096,4096)` | fp32 / 64 MiB | 32.134-57.424 ms | 0.0410-0.0871 ms | 368.8x |
| `(4096,4096)` | bf16 / 32 MiB | 10.301-34.715 ms | 0.0293-0.0418 ms | 351.2x |
| `(4096,8192)` | bf16 / 64 MiB | 16.896-22.184 ms | 0.0407-0.0617 ms | 273.7x |

The old MPS round-trip staged payload through CPU/NumPy in both directions.
The final `mlx_call` path aliases the Metal allocation through DLPack,
removing the payload-sized copies; the synchronized wrapper/barrier cost was
29-87 us across these repeats. The same-shape bf16 case is 32 MiB because each
element uses two bytes; the final row adds a true 64 MiB bf16 payload.

This zero-copy result applies to the scoped-borrow API, not to an MLX array
that must own its storage after the call. For that ownership contract, the
64 MiB fp32 materialized copy is about 4.08 ms versus about 60 us for a scoped
borrow. This is why the API separates owned and borrowed semantics instead of
exposing an unchecked `copy=False` default.

Final-API Sana 4-step E2E forced-MLX experiment using `mlx_call` for all 58
norms per DiT forward (clean paired repeat):

| Metric | Torch native | MLX scoped borrow | MLX penalty |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Denoising step median | 720.18 ms | 1170.40 ms | +62.5% |
| DiT forward median | 375.06 ms | 581.92 ms | +55.2% |
| Steady DiT median (drop first 2) | 353.42 ms | 581.92 ms | +64.7% |

A second same-configuration measurement had higher Torch variance and a
smaller penalty (+20.6% step, +21.9% DiT), but MLX was slower in both runs.

## Checklist

- [x] Formatted with repository pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Added and ran registered unit tests.
- [x] Registered the shared diffusion fallback in CPU CI.
- [x] Updated Apple Metal and diffusion documentation.
- [x] Included accuracy and speed evidence above.
- [x] CPU dependency pins remain unchanged.

## Review and Merge Process

This is a draft for review of the ownership contract and the diffusion path
decision. Please review the Torch/MLX lifetime semantics first; CI should run
the MLX, CPU, JIT-kernel, and multimodal-generation change paths before
promotion. In particular, the draft-gated MLX, Xeon CPU, and ARM64 CPU jobs
must complete before this PR is marked ready.

issues.title: [diffusion] fix: keep large vocab tables in host memory under layerwise offload
issues.body:
## Motivation

Layerwise offload streams a component's layers and then moves everything left over
to the device, on the reasonable assumption that the remainder is small — norms, a
patch embed, a time embed. For a text encoder it is not: umT5-XXL's token table is
`256384 x 4096` in fp32, so **3.91 GiB stays resident**, which on a 12 GiB card is a
third of the device.

That residency buys almost nothing. A vocab table is read by **gather, not GEMM** —
one row per token — so Wan's 512-token prompt touches 8 MiB of those 3.91 GiB, and it
does so once per request rather than once per denoising step:

| | |
|---|---|
| resident | 3.91 GiB |
| read per request | 512 x 4096 x 4 B = 8 MiB |
| utilisation | 0.2% |

Streaming it layer by layer would be worse still (3.91 GiB moved to read 8 MiB), so
the table belongs in host memory with the lookup running there and only the result
crossing PCIe.

This is what made `--performance-mode auto` unusable on a 12 GiB card: warmup at the
model's default workload had no headroom left and failed at every probe size.

## Modifications

Before the post-streaming `.to(device)`, swap tables above 256 MiB for placeholders;
restore them afterwards and hook the module so its input goes to the host and its
output comes back. Both call sites are covered — `LayerwiseOffloadManager._initialize`
and the multi-group path in `configure_layerwise_offload`.

Sharded tables are left alone: they are already divided by the world size, and their
output feeds an all-reduce that expects a device tensor.

## Accuracy Tests

Bit-exact. RTX 3060 12 GiB, `Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers`, layerwise offload of
dit/text_encoder/vae, 320x576, 9 frames, 8 steps, seed 1234 — **three runs each way,
six runs, one SHA-256** (`78a2a963...`).

New `test_host_resident_vocab_table.py` covers selection (large table picked, small
table, plain weight matrix and sharded table left alone), the detach/restore round
trip, and that the hooked gather matches a plain lookup — 7 tests. The existing
layerwise/offload/residency suites pass unchanged (136 tests together).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same runs, mean of three:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| peak VRAM | 8540 MiB | **4447 MiB** (-4.0 GiB, -48%) |
| `TextEncodingStage` | 3374.9 ms | 3384.4 ms (+0.28%) |
| total request | 13838.5 ms | 13815.8 ms |

The encode-stage cost is the CPU gather plus an 8 MiB host-to-device copy, once per
request. It does not separate from noise: the per-run ranges overlap (patched 3377–3389
vs baseline 3369–3382), and the total request is lower after the change. Peak VRAM is
also markedly steadier (4420–4500 vs 8000–9180).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

issues.body:
## Summary
- Centralize bit-exact first-sight `torch.equal` verify/disable behind `BitExactFusionGate` for FLUX / GLM / Sana / Ernie fused-norm sites (stops another per-model `_DISABLED/_VERIFIED` copy after #34126).
- Deduplicate shared helpers: Flux/Flux2/Qwen `_get_qkv_projections`, transformer lazy-load for denoising/Hunyuan3D, and route Z-Image RMSNorm wrappers through `fused_gate_rmsnorm`.
- Drop unused package-level `get_kernel` wrappers; keep registry entries for namespace discovery (including `sparse_linear_attn_fwd`).
- Rename generic native NSS symbols off the Qwen-only prefix; move `PRECISION_TO_TYPE` to a leaf `precision_types` module; refresh skill docs for `native_bf16_rmsnorm` / `BitExactFusionGate`.

## Why
Post-#34085 / #34126 parallel fast-path work left duplicated verify scaffolding, model-local helpers, dead package wrappers, and stale Qwen/Z-Image naming in code and skills. This cleanup keeps one implementation for each shared concern without changing numerical contracts.

## Impact
- No intended model-output, accuracy, or precision change.
- Bit-exact paths still self-verify on first sight and permanently fall back on mismatch.
- Unsupported shapes/dtypes/devices/compile contexts continue to use reference paths.
- JIT module/symbol names for native NSS change (`norm_scale_shift_native` / `nss_bf16_row`); cold rebuild expected on first use.

## Validation
- `python3 -m py_compile` on all touched Python modules.
- `ruff check --select F401,F841,F821,F811` on touched Python files: clean.
- Local smoke of `BitExactFusionGate` once/per-signature/mismatch paths.
- CUDA kernel/integration tests not re-run in this environment (no usable GPU / broken local `transformers`); rely on registered CI: `test_bitexact_gate`, `test_flux_ln_modulate`, `test_glm_image_ln_modulate`, `test_sana_ln_modulate`, `test_ernie_norm_scale_shift`, `test_kernels_namespace`.

issues.title: [diffusion] Sana: bit-exact fused aten LayerNorm+modulate under BCG (H200 denoise -4.8%)
issues.body:
> Rebased on main after #34008 merged — this PR now carries only the Sana changes (kernel generalization + wiring).

## Motivation

Sana's transformer runs the eager adaLN chain `LN(x) * (1 + scale) + shift` at
41 sites per DiT forward (norm1/norm2 in each of the 20 blocks + the final
`SanaModulatedNorm`), as 4 aten kernels per site (affine-free LayerNorm,
`1+scale` row op, broadcast mul, broadcast add) — and because the DiT
propagates the patch-embed/GLUMBConv `permute` layout, the LayerNorm pays a
hidden layout-copy on every call as well. Elementwise ops are ~51% of Sana's
per-step GPU time, and no existing fusion applies: the CuTe-DSL
norm+scale+shift family needs `hidden % 256 == 0`, while Sana's hidden is
2240 (70 heads x 32).

PR #34008 introduced a Triton kernel replicating torch's aten
`vectorized_layer_norm_kernel` numerics bit for bit (serial Welford in aten's
element order, guarded-rcp fast path, shfl.down combine tree, MUFU.RSQ, plus
the per-op bf16 rounding of the modulate chain), so the fusion needs no
quality gate. That kernel assumed `hidden % 512 == 0` (all 128 aten threads
run the same vector count).

## Changes

1. **Kernel** (`layernorm_modulate.py`)
   - Support any `hidden % 4 == 0` (aten's own vectorization requirement) via
     a masked partial tail chunk: aten threads whose next vector index
     `i*128 + t` reaches `N/4` skip the iteration and enter the warp fold
     with a smaller Welford count. The `hidden % 512 == 0` path compiles
     exactly as before (GLM-Image regression tests stay green).
   - `fused_layernorm_modulate_raw`: direct-call variant without the
     `torch.ops` dispatch (~40 us CPU per call). The registered custom op
     now wraps the raw function; GLM-Image call sites are unchanged.
   - num_warps heuristic extended to 4 from hidden >= 2048 (H200-tuned:
     14.3 us vs the 43.1 us eager chain at Sana's (2, 1024, 2240)).

2. **Sana** (`sana.py`): route the three LN+modulate sites through the fused
   kernel, but **only in CUDA-graph contexts** — under stream capture or on
   a non-default stream (which is where the breakable-CUDA-graph runner
   (#33989) warms up and captures). Each new input signature
   (shape/stride/dtype/eps) is `torch.equal`-verified against the live eager
   chain during the BCG warmup iterations (non-capturing, so the sync is
   legal); capture then records the fused kernel; any mismatch permanently
   falls back to eager (#34008 recipe).

   Default-stream eager serving deliberately keeps the eager chain: Sana's
   eager mode is CPU-launch bound, and one Triton launch costs more Python
   time than the whole 5-deep aten enqueue pipeline it replaces — an
   in-process alternating A/B on the real model measured +14% forward wall
   when fusing eagerly, despite -4.8% GPU kernel time. Under BCG replay the
   Python launch cost is zero and the GPU saving is realized in full.

   The wrapper also issues an explicit `x.contiguous()` (the same copy
   aten's LayerNorm performs internally for Sana's transposed activations),
   keeping the fused site at 2 kernels vs the eager 5.

## Correctness (H200, torch 2.11.0+cu130)

- Standalone sweep: `torch.equal` at D=2240 (tail path), 4096/2560
  (GLM-Image regression), 3072 (FLUX.1), 1536/708/452; batch 1/2;
  seq 1..4096 — all bit-exact.
- Unit tests: new `test_sana_ln_modulate.py` (4 cases: real serving shapes
  incl. the transposed layout; asserts eager serving stays on the eager
  chain and the fusion verifies + engages on the capture-stream path) +
  existing `test_glm_image_ln_modulate.py` = 10 passed.
- e2e md5: output PNGs bit-identical to main in every paired round, both
  configs (10 rounds x 10 images compared), plus a 2-prompt x 2-seed
  4-arm check.
- Trace audit: the eager arm is kernel-for-kernel identical to main
  (11136 launches, 0 fused); the BCG arm replays 492 fused launches and 0
  aten LN per 5-step window.

## Performance

GPU-side attribution (torch profiler, 5 denoise steps = 12 DiT forwards):

| arm | total GPU kernel | launches | aten LN | fused |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main BCG | 137.03 ms | 10932 | 492 | 0 |
| this PR BCG | 130.37 ms (-4.9%) | 9456 (-13.5%) | 0 | 492 |

(4 kernels per site -> 1 Triton kernel + the layout copy both arms already
paid.)

e2e, BCG config (protocol below): **denoise 405.2 -> 385.9 ms/request
(-4.8%)**, reproduced in 8/8 order-balanced paired rounds with spread
[-4.6%, -4.9%] across two builds. With denoise at ~55% of request e2e
(~0.74 s), this is ~-2.6% e2e. Wall/e2e/decode medians on this box swing
+-10-35% between *identical* binaries due to co-tenant load (measured with
a trace-identical build), so the graph-replayed denoise ratio is the
reliable metric; md5 identity plus the kernel-level trace deltas above are
the ground truth.

Eager config: unchanged by construction (trace-identical to main).

## Benchmark configuration

- H200 (ion8, shared box), torch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
- `Efficient-Large-Model/SANA1.5_1.6B_1024px_diffusers`, 1024x1024,
  seed 42, 20 steps (default preset), num_gpus=1, torch.compile off
- BCG arms: `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph --warmup-resolutions 1024x1024`
- 10 back-to-back requests per round in one warmed process, drop first,
  median of 9; rounds run interleaved main/PR in both orders (main-first
  and PR-first) to cancel co-tenant drift; per-round paired deltas
- md5 of every saved PNG compared main vs PR per round

## Dependency

Depends on #34008 — this branch contains its commit; the kernel file and
GLM-Image wiring come from there. New in this PR: the tail-chunk
generalization, the raw direct-call variant, the warp heuristic, and the
Sana wiring.

## Follow-up (FLUX.1, #34004)

The generalized kernel is bit-exact at FLUX.1's hidden=3072 too. Measured on
top of the #34004 branch at the FLUX image-stream shape (1, 4096, 3072):

| variant | time | bit-exact |
|---|---|---|
| eager 4-kernel chain | 87.7 us | ref |
| #34004 lossless (aten LN + fused modulate) | 38.4 us | yes |
| #34004 quality=high folded-affine LN | 27.2 us | no (maxdiff 1.3e-1) |
| this kernel, single launch | 23.8 us | yes |

i.e. it strictly dominates the quality=high folded site while staying
lossless (at the (1, 512, 3072) text stream it ties: 23.7 vs 19.5/25.0 us).
Caveat before wiring it there: FLUX eager serving needs the same
CPU-launch-bound check that gated Sana (Sana lesson: a Triton launch can
cost more Python than the aten chain it replaces).

issues.title: [Diffusion] Reuse shared AlignedVector and tidy jit_kernel/diffusion
issues.body:
## Motivation

The KDA-Pilot diffusion native-CUDA fast paths each need a 128-bit vectorized load/store. The first one that landed (`norm_scale_shift`, #27392) already uses the shared `device::AlignedVector` component from `sgl_kernel/vec.cuh`, but the two newer kernels (#29281, #29361) still hand-roll their own local `union`. This PR makes all the diffusion CUDA kernels reuse the shared `AlignedVector` component instead of a per-kernel `union`, and folds in a few small, verified cleanups found while reviewing the rest of `jit_kernel/diffusion/`. No behavior change.

## Modifications

**Native CUDA (`.cuh`) — reuse `device::AlignedVector`:**
- `residual_gate_add`: replace `union Vec16<T>` with `device::AlignedVector<T, kVec>` (`.load()`/`.store()`/`operator[]`).
- `causal_conv3d_cat_pad`: replace `union Pack` with `device::AlignedVector<ET, kVec>` (scattered scalar reads stay scalar `__ldg`; only the vectorized store changes).
- `timestep_embedding`: replace raw `float4` with `AlignedVector<float, 4>`, and add `#pragma once` + a named namespace `sglang_timestep_embedding` to match its siblings (plus the matching wrapper symbol in `timestep_embedding.py`).

**CuTe-DSL / Triton cleanups:**
- Hoist the byte-identical `to_cute_arg` / `to_fake_cute_args` helpers into `cutedsl/utils.py` and import them in both kernel files (removes ~36 duplicated lines).
- Fix a copy-paste guard in `norm_tanh_mul_add_norm_scale` (`isinstance(src, …) and isinstance(src, …)` → `… isinstance(dst, …)`, matching the sibling).
- Delete the dead `_precompute_inv_rms` in `sana_wm_gdn` (superseded by `fused_qk_inv_rms`; no callers).
- Drop the unused `rows` parameter from the `scale_shift` 4D kernel and its call site.
- Drop unused `B, S` args from `validate_weight_bias` (only `D` is used; matches the sibling signature).
- Remove stale commented-out code (`norm.py`, `scale_residual_norm_scale_shift.py`) and fix a stale docstring module name in `sana_wm_gdn`.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on B200 (`pytest`, all pass):
- `test/registered/jit/diffusion/{test_residual_gate_add, test_causal_conv3d_cat_pad, test_fused_norm_scale_shift, test_qwen_image_modulation}.py`
- `test/registered/jit/test_timestep_embedding.py`

A torch-reference smoke over every touched kernel (the 4 CuTe-DSL modulation entries, the 4D `scale_shift` path, `sana_wm_gdn.fused_qk_inv_rms`, plus a negative test that `validate_weight_bias` still rejects bad shapes) matches within bf16 tolerance.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Before/after on **B200**, OLD = `union`/`float4`, NEW = `AlignedVector` (`cuda` column from the registered benches; medians).

**`bench_residual_gate_add` — `cuda` µs (neutral):**

| workload | OLD | NEW |
|---|---:|---:|
| ltx2_bcast_s32640_c4096 | 126.35 | 125.97 |
| ltx2_full_s8160_c4096 | 41.64 | 41.65 |
| ideogram4_bcast_s4096_c4608 | 23.23 | 23.27 |
| flux2_bcast_s4608_c3072 | 16.02 | 16.05 |
| flux2_bcast_s512_c3072 | 15.93 | 15.68 |
| ltx2_full_s126_c2048 | 13.98 | 13.94 |

**`bench_causal_conv3d_cat_pad` — `cuda` µs (within noise):**

| case | OLD | NEW |
|---|---:|---:|
| c512_t4_h120_w208_cache1 | 126.98 | 129.02 |
| c512_t4_h120_w208_cache2 | 151.55 | 151.61 |
| c256_t4_h240_w416_cache1 | 230.4 | 232.4 |
| c256_t4_h240_w416_cache2 | 274.40 | 276.48 |

The conv3d numbers wobble <1%. To rule out a real regression I diffed the generated SASS of the bf16 `cat_pad_flat_kernel` (largest shape) for OLD vs NEW:

- **identical instruction count: 1184 vs 1184**
- **1× `STG` (a single 128-bit store) and 8× `LDG`** in both — i.e. `AlignedVector::store` lowers to the same `STG.128` as the old `uint4` union
- **0 local-memory ops (`STL`/`LDL` = 0)** in both — no register spilling
- only difference: a single `IMAD`↔`IADD3` scheduling swap (467/127 vs 468/126)

`ncu` agrees: same DRAM throughput (~18.5%), same SM throughput (~81%), zero local load/store sectors in both. The kernel is SM-issue-bound, so the sub-1% wall-clock difference is compiler-scheduling/measurement noise, not an algorithmic or memory regression.

`timestep_embedding` has no registered bench; it is a tiny vectorized store kernel covered by `test_timestep_embedding.py` (the `float4` → `AlignedVector<float,4>` change keeps a single 128-bit store).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (No new tests — behavior-preserving cleanup covered by existing diffusion unit tests.)
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

issues.title: [Diffusion] Fuse LTX2 qknorm split-RoPE
issues.body:
## Motivation

Fuse the LTX-2.3 attention Q/K RMSNorm + split-RoPE sequence into one Triton fast path.

This follows the optimization direction used by NVIDIA Sana's sol-engine branch:
[`NVlabs/Sana@00cb598`](https://github.com/NVlabs/Sana/tree/00cb59836c297bd5fad401000ee65f9042f29d02), specifically its LTX2 fused qknorm + split-RoPE path. This PR adapts the idea to SGLang's current native diffusion implementation and keeps SGLang's default guarded-fallback behavior.

The hot pattern in `LTX2Attention.forward` is:

```python
q = self.q_norm(q)
k = self.k_norm(k)
q = apply_split_rotary_emb(q, (cos, sin))
k = apply_split_rotary_emb(k, (k_cos, k_sin))
```

For LTX-2.3 HQ, this appears in both stage-1 denoising and stage-2 refinement, including large split-RoPE rows such as the stage-2 packed video latent shape `[1, 32640, 128]`.

## Modifications

- Add `sglang.jit_kernel.diffusion.triton.ltx2_qknorm.ltx2_qknorm_split_rope_pair`.
- Fuse Q and K RMSNorm with split-RoPE in a pair kernel for BF16 `[batch, seq, hidden]` tensors.
- Wire `LTX2Attention.forward` to try the fused path before the existing separate RMSNorm + split-RoPE path.
- Keep the path default-on but narrowly guarded:
  - TP world size must be 1.
  - `q_norm` / `k_norm` must be `torch.nn.RMSNorm`.
  - Q/K and split-RoPE tensors must be CUDA BF16 with the expected contiguous/4D split-RoPE layout.
  - Unsupported shapes or dtypes fall back to the existing implementation.
  - Runtime kernel failure disables this fast path for the process and logs a `warning_once`.
- Add CUDA correctness coverage for same-seq and different-seq Q/K shapes plus interleaved-RoPE fallback.

## Accuracy Tests

Local:

```bash
python3 -m py_compile \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/ltx_2.py \
  python/sglang/jit_kernel/diffusion/triton/ltx2_qknorm.py \
  test/registered/jit/diffusion/test_ltx2_qknorm_split_rope.py
python3 -m ruff format --check \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/ltx_2.py \
  python/sglang/jit_kernel/diffusion/triton/ltx2_qknorm.py \
  test/registered/jit/diffusion/test_ltx2_qknorm_split_rope.py
python3 -m ruff check \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/ltx_2.py \
  python/sglang/jit_kernel/diffusion/triton/ltx2_qknorm.py \
  test/registered/jit/diffusion/test_ltx2_qknorm_split_rope.py
git diff --check
```

Result: all checks passed.

B200:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 \
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/sglang_qknorm_split_rope_validate/python:/tmp/sglang_qknorm_split_rope_validate \
FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \
pytest -q test/registered/jit/diffusion/test_ltx2_qknorm_split_rope.py -s
```

Result: `3 passed, 20 warnings`.

## Speed Tests

B200 model E2E benchmark:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 \
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/sglang_qknorm_split_rope_<impl>/python:/tmp/sglang_qknorm_split_rope_<impl> \
FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \
sglang generate \
  --backend=sglang \
  --model-path=Lightricks/LTX-2.3 \
  --pipeline-class-name=LTX2TwoStageHQPipeline \
  --ltx2-two-stage-device-mode original \
  --prompt="A beautiful sunset over the ocean" \
  --seed=42 \
  --width=1920 --height=1088 --num-frames=121 \
  --num-inference-steps=15 \
  --save-output --warmup \
  --perf-dump-path /tmp/ltx23_qknorm_split_rope_e2e/<impl>/perf.json \
  --output-file-path /tmp/ltx23_qknorm_split_rope_e2e/<impl>/<impl>.mp4
```

- Host: `ion-b200`, NVIDIA B200, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7`.
- Main commit: `5996b54bd3`; PR commit: `4e94cb0792`.
- Model path: `Lightricks/LTX-2.3`, native `LTX2TwoStageHQPipeline`.
- Shape: T2V `1920x1088x121f`, recommended HQ `num_inference_steps=15`, `seed=42`.
- Measurement: `sglang generate --warmup`; metric is `perf.json` `total_duration_ms`, with the warmup request excluded.
- Backend gate: both logs show `Using explicitly specified pipeline: LTX2TwoStageHQPipeline`; no diffusers fallback was observed.
- Fast-path stability gate: no `Disabling LTX2 fused q/k norm + split-RoPE` warning was observed.

| Implementation | E2E ms | LTX2AVDenoisingStage ms | LTX2RefinementStage ms | LTX2AVDecodingStage ms | Peak reserved MB | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main | 46737.57 | 29851.18 | 12749.93 | 3692.71 | 67902 | 1.000x |
| Fused qknorm + split-RoPE | 46316.99 | 29493.81 | 12661.86 | 3711.42 | 67902 | **1.009x (+0.91%)** |

## B200 Visual Output Check

Visual equivalence check uses the same full LTX-2.3 HQ command as the model benchmark above.

- Host/GPU: `ion-b200`, NVIDIA B200, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7`.
- Main commit: `5996b54bd3`; PR commit: `4e94cb0792`.
- Prompt/shape: `A beautiful sunset over the ocean`, `1920x1088x121f`, recommended HQ `num_inference_steps=15`, `seed=42`.
- Native `LTX2TwoStageHQPipeline` was used for both runs; no diffusers fallback was observed.
- Decoded-video comparison: SSIM All `0.984495`, PSNR average `39.982356 dB`.

Left is `main`; right is this PR:

![LTX-2.3 HQ main vs fused qknorm split-RoPE visual comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-ltx2-qknorm-split-rope-assets/ltx2-qknorm-split-rope/assets/main_vs_qknorm_split_rope.gif)

MP4 artifacts: [main.mp4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-ltx2-qknorm-split-rope-assets/ltx2-qknorm-split-rope/main/main.mp4), [pr.mp4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-ltx2-qknorm-split-rope-assets/ltx2-qknorm-split-rope/qknorm_split_rope/qknorm_split_rope.mp4), [side-by-side.mp4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-ltx2-qknorm-split-rope-assets/ltx2-qknorm-split-rope/assets/main_vs_qknorm_split_rope.mp4).

## Checklist

- [x] Sana sol-engine optimization source acknowledged.
- [x] Default path tries fused qknorm + split-RoPE and falls back safely.
- [x] No environment variable is required to enable the fast path.
- [x] B200 CUDA correctness test included.

issues.title: [Diffusion] Fuse LTX2 RMS AdaLN modulation
issues.body:
## Motivation

Fuse the repeated LTX-2.3 RMSNorm + AdaLN modulation pattern:

```python
norm_hidden_states = rms_norm(hidden_states) * (1 + scale) + shift
```

The LTX-2.3 HQ transformer hits this pattern in video/audio self-attention, prompt cross-attention, and MLP preparation. This PR follows the same LTX2 RMS AdaLN fusion opportunity used by NVlabs/Sana `sol-engine` at commit `00cb59836c297bd5fad401000ee65f9042f29d02`.

Unlike Sana's local Triton `ltx2_rms_norm_modulate` kernel, SGLang main already has a generic CUDA/CuTe DSL `sglang::fused_norm_scale_shift` primitive with RMSNorm and `[B, 1, D]` scale/shift broadcast support. This PR wires LTX2 into that existing primitive instead of adding another model-local kernel.

## Modifications

- Add a default-on LTX2 fused RMS AdaLN helper around `fused_norm_scale_shift(..., norm_type="rms")`.
- Keep no user-facing environment variable; unsupported shapes/devices/dtypes fall back to the original PyTorch expression.
- Disable the fused path for the current process after a runtime launch failure, then continue with the original path.
- Use the fused helper for LTX2 video/audio self-attention, prompt cross-attention, and MLP RMS AdaLN sites.
- Leave A2V/V2A dual modulation untouched, since that belongs to the separate dual-modulate fusion.
