issues.title: [Feat] diffusion/openai: Cancel video jobs on DELETE
issues.body:
## Motivation

`DELETE /v1/videos/{id}` removes the job record, but the job keeps its GPU until it finishes (`# TODO: support aborting a job`). A client that cancels a long video job still blocks the replica for the full run.

This revives #24547 by @qimcis, which was approved but no longer applies to main, with a smaller scope:

- a queued job does not start;
- a running job stops after its current denoising step.

Removing one cancelled request from a running dynamic batch is left for a follow-up.

## Modifications

**Cancel channel.** A replica driver runs the forward on the thread that reads its request socket, so it cannot read a cancel while a job runs. The HTTP server now publishes each cancelled request id on a ZMQ XPUB socket with `XPUB_NODROP` backpressure (`entrypoints/openai/video_cancel.py`). This is the reverse of the progress channel from #45919, with the same deployment limits (monolithic, single node). Each driver subscribes and reads the ids at each check (`managers/request_cancel.py`), and drains them in the scheduler receive loop while idle. DELETE returns a retryable 503 and retains the job if a replica has not subscribed or the transport is full.

**All ranks stop at the same step.** The driver broadcasts its decision on the replica CPU (gloo) group. In #24547 each rank checked a marker file on its own, so with sequence parallelism one rank could stop at step k while the others waited in a collective of step k+1. The broadcast runs on the CPU group, so it adds no GPU sync.

**Check points.**
- Before dynamic merging in the scheduler and before the forward in `GPUWorker`, so observed queued cancellations do not enter a mixed live batch. Explicit request groups retain their single-reply protocol.
- After each denoising step, through `PipelineStage.progress_bar`. Every denoising loop advances it once per step, so no loop needs its own edit. Stages that run on the main rank only get no step check, because the check is a collective.
- The sequential path (multi-output SANA-Video 2.0 jobs, and native grouped requests) runs the first stage once for the group. There the worker checks each request before the group starts and runs only the requests that are not cancelled, so each request keeps its own output. The executor also checks before each output, so after a cancel the outputs that remain stop at once.

**DELETE after a timeout.** DELETE publishes cancellation for unfinished jobs, including jobs that `--scheduler-rpc-timeout` marked failed: the timeout ends the HTTP wait, not the GPU work. Completed jobs can be removed without a cancellation channel. The listener retains a bounded history of cancelled IDs.

**Dynamic batches.** A merged batch is cancellable only when each member is, and it stops only when each member is cancelled. The other members continue. The scheduler checks `OutputBatch.cancelled` before `OutputBatch.error`, in the merged batch and in the native grouped batch, so a stopped batch returns cancelled outputs, not errors.

**Logs.** A cancelled request is logged once at info level (`Stopped request ...`). It is not logged as an error with a traceback on each rank. `OutputBatch.cancelled` lets the HTTP side tell a cancel from a failure. `RequestCancelledError` is in the leaf module `request_cancel_error`, so the logging and profiling utilities import it at module level.

The docs for `DELETE /v1/videos/{id}` are updated.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: the change does not touch model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Requests other than cancellable `/v1/videos` jobs, and warmup requests, do not run per-step cancellation checks. The driver still drains the control channel in the scheduler receive loop. For a video job, each denoising step adds one non-blocking ZMQ read on the driver and, on a multi-rank replica, one broadcast of one int32 on the gloo CPU group.

Microbenchmark of the per-step check on CPU (Apple M5 Pro, Python 3.14, torch 2.14, 5000 iterations after 500 warmup iterations; local processes over loopback):

| Per-step work | mean | p50 | p99 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CancelListener.is_cancelled`, no cancel received | 15 us | 16 us | 25 us |
| gloo broadcast of one int32, 2 ranks | 51 us | 49 us | 97 us |
| gloo broadcast of one int32, 4 ranks | 80 us | 76 us | 151 us |
| gloo broadcast of one int32, 8 ranks | 149 us | 146 us | 238 us |

With 8 ranks the check adds about 0.17 ms per step: 0.02 percent of a 1 s MiniMax-H3 step, 0.3 percent of a 50 ms step. The broadcast also makes the CPU thread of each rank wait for the driver once per step, so no rank can queue more than one step of kernels ahead of the driver. A replica across nodes pays the TCP round trip instead of loopback. These initial measurements did not include a matched GPU end-to-end comparison; see the maintainer follow-up below. In the GPU test below, an 8-step MiniMax-H3 job took 9 s with the change. If a maintainer prefers, the check can run every N steps; it cannot use a time interval, because every rank must call the broadcast at the same step.

## Test

**Unit tests** (`test/unit/test_request_cancel.py`, CPU):
- publisher to listener over ipc, ids of expanded outputs (`job:0`), the size bound of the id set;
- a two-process gloo test: every rank follows the driver's decision, also when its own view differs (this test fails when the broadcast is removed);
- the step check stops a loop through `ReportingTqdm`, and only replicated stages get the check;
- the worker skips the forward of a cancelled request;
- the sequential path: a cancelled request does not start and the other requests keep their outputs, the outputs after a cancel stop at once without an error log, and a merged multi-output result stays cancelled;
- DELETE publishes the cancel, also after a scheduler RPC timeout, and a deleted job is not marked failed;
- the dynamic-batch merge rule, and a stopped merged or native grouped batch returns cancelled outputs with no error log;
- `init_request_cancel`, `cancel_endpoint`, and the lifespan start and stop of the publisher;
- each new module imports first without an import cycle.

**GPU test** (covers the per-step and queued checks, not the sequential path; MiniMax-H3 ref2va, 8 x H100, `--ulysses-degree 8 --quantization fp8`, this branch over `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261026`):

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| DELETE a running 50-step job at 10 percent | All 8 ranks stopped after step 6. The next job started 1.1 s after the DELETE and completed. |
| DELETE a job queued behind another job | It never ran. The next job started 1.0 s after the job ahead of it ended. |
| `/health` after the cancels | 200, no NCCL errors |
| Server log after startup | 0 tracebacks, 0 error lines |

## Limits

- A model whose denoising loop does not advance a progress bar runs to the end after a DELETE.
- Stages after denoising (for example decoding) do not run for a cancelled job. A job deleted after its last denoising step still decodes and saves or uploads its output, but the API does not return it.
- DELETE returns 503 with `Retry-After: 1` when the cancellation transport is full or not all replica drivers are subscribed. Retry with the same job ID; the API record is retained.
- An accepted command is not a worker acknowledgement. Cancellation remains best effort across process failures and eviction from the latest 4096 cancelled IDs. There is no durable cancellation protocol.
- Disaggregated and multi-node serving remain unsupported for cancellation; DELETE there only removes the API record.

## Maintainer follow-up (2026-10-29)

Commit `66320508ee15eee776f6fc8909b81e884386e53c` fixes the two reproduced review issues: queued cancellation before dynamic merging, and silent cancellation loss when PUB/SUB reaches its high-water mark. It also preserves explicit-group and deferred/streaming reply semantics, and drains idle replica listeners to avoid blocking cancellation on active replicas.

Validation on Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, diffusers 0.37.0 and pyzmq 27.2.0:

- Six targeted test files: **190 passed, 3 skipped**. The skipped two-GPU output-finalization test was separately rerun on CUDA and passed; the other two skips are inapplicable synchronous-caller variants.
- Real IPC coverage includes a 3500-command burst, accepted-command delivery and rejected-command retry, replica subscription/disconnect, DELETE failure preserving the job, and idle listener draining. Dynamic batching uses the real Wan batching contract with a fake model forward.
- Native Wan2.1 T2V 1.3B on **2 x H200, Ulysses 2**, BF16/resident weights, FA, eager, 832x480, 17 frames, seed 42. Stage-profiling synchronization was disabled. The same warm process alternated cancellation checks off/on in A-B-B-A order, eight samples per arm, with progress reporting and output saving enabled in both arms. Median saved-output E2E: **0.812 s off / 0.816 s on (+0.5%)**. This isolates the check toggle, not the entire branch versus main, and is not a throughput or all-model guarantee.
- A 50-step request cancelled after progress step 20 stopped at step 21 without decode; a pre-cancelled request did not enter the pipeline. The next normal request completed, and all 17 comparable MP4s were byte-identical (SHA-256 `303bbf16219dbff03d36f81a92739fdc446fd9eded0aa85e467fb72c6854c426`).
- GPU validation exercised the real scheduler/process/collective path through a diagnostic SDK harness. DELETE-to-transport integration is covered separately by the IPC tests; this is not an additional live HTTP E2E test. The diagnostic SDK reports cancelled outputs as errors because it is not the public async cancellation API. Shutdown also emitted a CUDA IPC producer-lifetime warning, which is not claimed fixed here.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks pass.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Remove per-step host syncs and uploads in video models
issues.body:
Depends on #46045 (host-sync guards in `test/unit/host_sync_guard.py`); this branch is stacked on it.

## Motivation

Video pipelines run long denoising loops where every blocking host read or pageable upload stalls the host on the previous step's kernels, and several of them rebuilt request-constant RoPE tables or masks on every forward. This PR removes those per-step costs model by model. Outputs are bitwise unchanged.

## Modifications

- **MOVA** (`model_specific_stages/mova.py`, `bridges/mova_dual_tower.py`): the loop uploaded both timesteps every step and `step_from_to` read them back with `float()`, four syncs per step. The paired schedule is uploaded once and the scheduler steps on the host values. Every forward re-uploaded both towers' CPU complex128 RoPE tables (six blocking copies, ~17 MB for audio) and redid the full-sequence concats, and every bridge layer rebuilt its fp32 cos/sin caches (30 layers x 2 directions); tables and bridge caches are built once per request and freed when the loop ends.
- **MiniMax-H3 / FastH3** (`dits/minimax_h3.py`, `minimax_h3_adaln_cache.py`): FastH3 PDD heads copied that step's weight and bias from the host stacks, four blocking copies per step; the stacks are uploaded once per (device, dtype) and indexed by step. The AdaLN online cache indexed its slabs with a 0-dim device slot (a host read, two per step); it now gathers with `index_select` and keeps the old strides.
- **HunyuanVideo** (`dits/hunyuanvideo.py`): the forward built the RoPE cos/sin on the host and copied both to the device every forward (~59 MB per step at 720p x 125 frames). The uploaded tables are kept per request in an underscore `Req.extra` key, which the disaggregation transport skips.
- **Helios** (`helios_denoising.py`, `dits/helios.py`): frame indices were built on the host and uploaded by each of four RoPE embeddings per forward (eight syncs per CFG step); they are built on the latent device. Every block cast the full-sequence [B, L, 6, D] modulation to fp32 (~1.4 GB per block at 384x640); the compact rows are cast once before the expand/concat.
- **Wan family** (`dits/causal_wanvideo.py`, `dits/wanvideo.py`): causal Wan (LongLive2) copied its host RoPE tables to the device every forward; they are uploaded once per request and chunk position. Wan and causal Wan blocks each cast the batch-wide modulation to fp32; the forward casts it once (the per-token TI2V table keeps its fused bf16 path).
- **LTX-2** (`dits/ltx_2.py`, `ltx_2/denoising.py`; paths not touched by #45966): `prepare_video_coords` uploaded two constant tensors per call (every forward on the LTX-2.3 one-stage path, every step for JoyEcho memory coords); they are uploaded once per device. HQ res2s: the SDE coefficient NaN replacement went through a 0-dim boolean index (nonzero on get and set, four calls per step) and is now a `torch.where`; the 100-iteration bongmath refinement hoists its fp64 casts and `h * a21`; the stage-1 step size starts from the step's host sigmas instead of `.cpu()` reads.
- **JoyEcho** (`joy_echo/denoising.py`): every DMD step read sigma and sigma_next with `.item()`; the loop takes fp32 host and device copies of the schedule once. With the memory bank (shot >= 2) the shot-constant cross masks, audio block mask and memory RoPE coords are built once per loop instead of every step.
- **SANA-WM / SANA-Video2** (`sana_wm*.py`, `sana_wm/streaming*.py`, `sana_video2.py`): the cache-type flag was uploaded in every block's clean pass and read back by the next chunk (20 uploads + 20 reads per chunk) and is now a host tensor; self-forcing steps read their timestep once per chunk; `forward_long` windows camera/Plucker inputs once per chunk so the UCPE and Plucker caches hit; the UCPE invalid-ray fix is a `torch.where`; the chunked refiner reads its sigmas from a host copy and builds each block's RoPE once on the device. SANA-Video2 builds its RoPE tables once per latent shape instead of uploading complex128 tables twice per forward.
- **Cosmos3 world models** (`dits/cosmos_dreams.py`, `dits/cosmos3_sim_auto.py`, `cosmos3_simulation/sim_auto.py`): Dreams zeroed null-action V slots by indexing with a Python list in each of 36 layers (a blocking upload each); the slots are per-frame slices. Sim-Auto's scatter/gather indexes, mRoPE frame ids and generated-frame masks are built once per chunk on the device. The default Cosmos3 T2V/I2V loop is untouched (#45967 covers its CFG window).

Tests:
- `test_mova_denoising.py`: steps never upload or read device timesteps (`SyncOnRead` schedule, one upload); RoPE tables built once per request; outputs bitwise equal.
- `test_minimax_h3_pdd_offline.py`, `test_minimax_h3_adaln_cache.py`: heads uploaded once; slab gathers run under `forbid_host_syncs` with the old values and strides.
- `test_hunyuanvideo_rope_upload.py`, `test_wan_step_host_overhead.py`: RoPE tables uploaded once per request (per chunk position for causal Wan), identical tables; blocks receive fp32 modulation.
- `test_helios_step_host_overhead.py`: frame indices live on the latent device; blocks receive fp32 modulation.
- `test_ltx2_step_host_overhead.py`: video-coord constants uploaded once; SDE coefficients under `forbid_host_syncs`; the refinement casts once.
- `test_joy_echo_denoising_host_overhead.py`: host/device sigma copies, steps never read device sigmas, the memory prefix is built once.
- `sana_wm/test_host_overhead.py`, `test_sana_video2.py`, `test_cosmos3_simulation_host_overhead.py`, `test_cosmos_dreams.py`, `test_cosmos3_sim_auto.py`: the SANA-WM, SANA-Video2 and Cosmos3 world-model paths above.

No hunk overlaps #45942, #45943, #45944, #45948, #45965, #45966, #45967, #45977, #45978, #45979 or #45987; each of them still applies on top of this branch.

## Accuracy Tests

2xH200, eager profiles, two requests per model with different inputs. Decoded frames (and audio where the model produces it) are bitwise identical to main:

| model (request) | GPUs | outputs compared | main vs PRs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I 1024x1024, 40 steps | 1 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 edit 1024x1024, 40 steps | 1 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Z-Image-Turbo 1024x1024, 9 steps, TP2 | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| FLUX.3 Klein Base 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Ideogram-4 FP8 1024x1024, 20 steps, TP2 | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2I 1280x720, 35 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2V 1280x720x61, 35 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| HunyuanVideo 848x480x61, 30 steps, Ulysses 2 | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| LTX-2 two-stage 768x512x121, 40 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B 1280x720x33, 40 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| MiniMax-H3 T2VA 1344x768 4 s, 12 steps, Ulysses 2 | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |
| MOVA-360p I2VA 640x352x97, 20 steps, TP2 | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Host syncs inside the denoising stage per step (rank 0, `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("warn")` around the stage, real server requests):

| model (request) | main: per step in the loop / per request | this PR: per step in the loop / per request |
|---|---|---|
| HunyuanVideo 848x480x61, 30 steps, Ulysses 2 | 4 / 121 | 0 / 3 |
| MOVA-360p I2VA 640x352x97, 20 steps, TP2 | 16 / 320 | 0 / 13 |
| LTX-2 two-stage, stage 1, 768x512x121, 40 steps, CFG parallel | 4 / 161 | 2 / 81 (the sigma reads #45966 removes) |
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B 1280x720x33, 40 steps, CFG parallel | 0 / 2 | 0 / 2 |
| MiniMax-H3 T2VA (fl2va) 1344x768 4 s, 12 steps, Ulysses 2 | 0 / 38 | 0 / 38 (setup; the FastH3 PDD and AdaLN-cache paths are not in this command) |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2V 1280x720x61, 35 steps, CFG parallel | 0 / 7 | 0 / 7 |

Client latency, interleaved A/B (main, PR, PR, main), fresh server per run, median of 2 measured requests per run:

| cell | round | main | this PR (with #46045) |
|---|---|---|---|
| MOVA-360p I2VA 640x352x97, 20 steps, TP2 | 1 | 46.696 s | 46.458 s |
| | 2 | 46.706 s | 46.524 s |
| | median | 46.701 s | 46.491 s (-0.45%) |
| HunyuanVideo 848x480x61, 30 steps, Ulysses 2 | 1 | 46.120 s | 46.122 s |
| | 2 | 46.158 s | 46.096 s |
| | median | 46.139 s | 46.109 s (-0.07%, noise) |

- MOVA: the denoising stage went from 44.67 s to 44.22 s (-1.0%) in both rounds, from the 16 per-step syncs and the per-forward RoPE rebuilds going away.
- HunyuanVideo at this shape is GPU-bound (about 1.4 s per step), so the four removed syncs per step do not show in the latency; the saving is the per-step 2 x RoPE upload, which grows with resolution and frame count.
- Wan2.2-T2V-A14B and MiniMax-H3 T2VA have no per-step syncs on main in these commands (table above), so no latency change is expected there; their A/B did not complete (the benchmark machine was released mid-run, after one MiniMax-H3 main run at 138.38 s). This needs a rerun before the speed claim covers them.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

issues.title: [Feat] diffusion: Native SANA-Sprint support
issues.body:
## Motivation

Closes #43671. Joint work with @raghulchandramouli, who independently found the SANA 1.5 qk_norm bug on #43671; his commits are listed under *Joint contributions*.

[SANA-Sprint 0.6B](https://huggingface.co/Efficient-Large-Model/Sana_Sprint_0.6B_1024px_diffusers) is a guidance-distilled SANA variant that generates 1024px images in 1–4 steps. Its checkpoint declares `SanaSprintPipeline` and `SCMScheduler`, and neither had a native implementation. This reuses the SANA transformer, Gemma2 encoder and DC-AE, and adds Sprint's pipeline, scheduler and defaults.

## Modifications

- **`SCMScheduler`** (`runtime/models/schedulers/scheduling_scm.py`): subclasses Diffusers' TrigFlow sCM scheduler. Diffusers' `SanaSprintPipeline` does three things inline in its loop: it rescales the DiT input, converts the DiT's flow prediction to TrigFlow, and divides the final sample by `sigma_data`. Here `scale_model_input` / `step` / `init_noise_sigma` do that work, so the shared `DenoisingStage` loop runs Sprint unchanged. `timesteps` holds the sCM timesteps the DiT is conditioned on. The 2-step intermediate angle (1.3) is applied only for 2 steps, so 1/3/4 steps work without passing `intermediate_timesteps=None` as Diffusers requires.
- **SANA DiT** (`runtime/models/dits/sana.py`):
  - `guidance_embeds` checkpoints get `SanaCombinedTimestepGuidanceEmbeddings`, with Diffusers' module layout and weight names.
  - `qk_norm="rms_norm_across_heads"` is now applied in both the linear self-attention and the cross-attention.
  - The arch default for `qk_norm` changes to `None`, matching Diffusers. SANA 1.0 configs omit the key and have no norm weights.
- **Pipeline** (`runtime/pipelines/sana_sprint.py`, `configs/pipeline_configs/sana_sprint.py`, `configs/sample/sana_sprint.py`):
  - Sprint's "complex human instruction" prompt prefix. It reuses SANA-Video's text stage; the instruction is now a class attribute there, and SANA-Video's behavior is unchanged.
  - Per-request embedded guidance: `guidance_scale × guidance_embeds_scale`, rounded to the DiT dtype as Diffusers does.
  - fp32 latents.
  - Defaults: 2 steps, `guidance_scale=4.5`. CFG never runs, so negative prompts are ignored.
  - **Resolution binning**, on by default as in Diffusers (`use_resolution_binning`). The DiT runs at the closest 1024px aspect-ratio bin, then a Sprint decoding stage resizes and center-crops the image back to the requested size. The bin table copies Diffusers' `ASPECT_RATIO_1024_BIN`: importing it pulls in the whole PixArt pipeline (about 8.5 s), so a unit test asserts the copy still matches.
  - **Schedule overrides** per request: `max_timesteps`, `intermediate_timesteps` and explicit `trigflow_timesteps` (`num_inference_steps + 1` decreasing angles). They are validated at admission (a bad schedule returns HTTP 400: angles must lie in [0, 1.5708], explicit schedules must end at 0, and an explicit `intermediate_timesteps` applies only to 2 steps) and declared in `image_request_extra_fields`, so the image API forwards them. Diffusers 0.37's own custom-`timesteps` path raises a `TypeError`, because `retrieve_timesteps` omits `num_inference_steps` for `SCMScheduler`, so explicit angles are checked against Diffusers' scheduler directly.
  - The SANA detector excludes Sprint ids, and `sana_sprint` registers before generic SANA.
- **Tests:**
  - `test/unit/test_sana_sprint.py` (CPU).
  - 1-GPU server cases `sana_sprint_0.6b_t2i` and `sana_sprint_1.6b_t2i` with component accuracy enabled. Perf and consistency checks are off, as for `sana_video_2b_t2v`.
  - A component-accuracy hook branch: Sprint's DiT takes the same guidance value as Diffusers, not the FLUX-style ×1000.
- **Component-accuracy harness fix** (`component_accuracy/utils.py`): `normalize_state_key` rewrites `scale` to `weight`, which turned DC-AE's `to_qkv_multiscale.*` into `to_qkv_multiweight.*`. Prefix-stripped and suffix candidates were built only from that rewritten name, so 36 of 375 VAE parameters never transferred and any DC-AE case failed at 90.4% matched. Candidates are now derived from the original name too; when the two names are equal, the candidate order is unchanged.
- **Docs:** SANA-Sprint entry in the model catalog.

### Side effect: SANA 1.5 now loads its QK-norm weights

SANA 1.5 checkpoints ship trained `attn1/attn2.norm_q/norm_k` weights in every block. sglang's SANA DiT had no such parameters, so the loader skipped those weights with a warning and served the model without QK-norm. With this PR they load. DiT output against Diffusers' `SanaTransformer2DModel` on `SANA1.5_1.6B_1024px_diffusers` (real weights, fixed random inputs, bf16):

| | `norm_q`/`norm_k` params | rel. L2 vs Diffusers | cosine |
|---|---|---|---|
| upstream main | 0 | 25.0% | 0.969 |
| this PR | 80 | 3.5% | 0.9994 |

SANA 1.0 (600M / 1600M) is unaffected: no `qk_norm` in config, so no norm modules are built.

### Joint contributions from raghulchandramouli

- **SANA-Sprint 1.6B** (`Sana_Sprint_1.6B_1024px_diffusers`) is registered by exact id next to 0.6B, in the registry, the registry test and the model catalog. Its configs differ from 0.6B only in transformer size.
- **`test/unit/test_sana_dit_param_names.py`** (CPU) builds the native and Diffusers DiTs on the meta device for six real configs (SANA 1.0 600M/1600M, SANA 1.5 1.6B/4.8B, Sprint 0.6B/1.6B) and runs the loader's own name mapping. It asserts that every checkpoint weight lands on a native parameter of the same shape, and that no native parameter is left unloaded. Against main's DiT, the four configs with qk_norm or guidance embeddings fail; SANA 1.0 passes.
- **Scheduler review and schedule validation fixes.** Out-of-range TrigFlow angles used to reach the DiT (for example, `max_timesteps=2.3562` gave a timestep of about -9e4) and are now rejected at admission. An explicit `intermediate_timesteps` with steps other than 2 used to be dropped silently and is now rejected, as in Diffusers. The review also led to the `pred_original_sample` note in `SCMScheduler.step`'s docstring.

## Test

**Scheduler:** `test_scm_scheduler_reproduces_diffusers_sprint_loop` runs a deterministic stand-in for the bf16 DiT through Diffusers' `SanaSprintPipeline` loop and through the shared-loop call order, for 1, 2 and 4 steps. The outputs match bit for bit (`atol=0`). While writing it I caught a dtype issue: a 0-dim fp32 coefficient times a bf16 DiT output stays bf16, which drifted by about 1e-2. The scheduler now upcasts explicitly, and the test fails if that upcast is removed.

**Component accuracy, 0.6B (1-GPU harness):** all three checks pass. Before the harness fix above, the VAE check failed on weight transfer.

| component | CosSim vs Diffusers/HF |
|---|---|
| transformer (with guidance + qk_norm) | 0.999985 |
| text encoder (Gemma2) | 0.999829 |
| VAE (DC-AE) | 0.999781 |

**End to end vs Diffusers, 0.6B** (`SanaSprintPipeline`, bf16 DiT, VAE upcast to fp32 to match sglang). Same seed (42), 1024×1024, `guidance_scale=4.5`, image PSNR:

| prompt | 1 step | 2 steps | 4 steps |
|---|---|---|---|
| a tiny astronaut hatching from an egg on the moon | 37.0 dB | 33.8 dB | 36.9 dB |
| a red fox sitting in fresh snow, golden hour, photorealistic | 37.3 dB | 42.6 dB | 40.3 dB |
| an isometric illustration of a cozy library with plants and warm lamps | 27.4 dB | 27.7 dB | 28.1 dB |

**Resolution binning and schedule overrides vs Diffusers** (fox prompt, seed 42, 2 steps):

| request | output size (sglang = Diffusers) | PSNR |
|---|---|---|
| 1000×700 (bin 1216×832, resized back) | 700×1000 | 39.2 dB |
| 800×1200 | 1200×800 | 33.8 dB |
| 960×640 | 640×960 | 39.2 dB |
| `intermediate_timesteps=1.1` | 1024×1024 | 41.1 dB |

Over HTTP, explicit `trigflow_timesteps=[1.5708, 1.3, 0]` reproduces the default 2-step image bit for bit. A custom 4-angle schedule produces a clean image. A malformed schedule returns 400 with the reason.

The third prompt is the most detailed image; it keeps the same composition, with fine-detail differences. I traced the gap: there is no single divergence point. Each block differs from Diffusers by about 0.3% (bf16 rounding), and the 28 blocks amplify that to about 7% at the output. Diffusers' own bf16 DiT is just as far from its fp32 run:

| DiT input (real, from the pipeline) | Diffusers bf16 vs fp32 | sglang bf16 vs fp32 | sglang vs Diffusers (bf16) |
|---|---|---|---|
| prompt 1 | 5.0% | 5.5% | 3.8% |
| prompt 3 | 10.1% | 10.2% | 6.9% |

So sglang's output is as close to fp32 as Diffusers' bf16 path is. Switching sglang's linear attention to Diffusers' fp32 formulation, or the caption RMSNorm eps to 1e-5, does not reduce the gap.

**Component accuracy, 1.6B** (1-GPU harness, RTX A6000): all three checks pass.

| component | CosSim vs Diffusers/HF |
|---|---|
| transformer (with guidance + qk_norm) | 0.999979 |
| text encoder (Gemma2) | 0.999829 |
| VAE (DC-AE) | 0.999781 |

**End to end vs Diffusers, 1.6B** (same setup as 0.6B), image PSNR:

| prompt | 1 step | 2 steps | 4 steps |
|---|---|---|---|
| a tiny astronaut hatching from an egg on the moon | 30.0 dB | 26.7 dB | 28.3 dB |
| a red fox sitting in fresh snow, golden hour, photorealistic | 26.2 dB | 26.5 dB | 25.3 dB |
| an isometric illustration of a cozy library with plants and warm lamps | 29.0 dB | 26.7 dB | 28.0 dB |

1.6B scores lower than 0.6B, but the images keep the same composition, pose and lighting and differ only in fine texture. Against an fp32 Diffusers reference (`SanaSprintPipeline` in fp32, TF32 off), both bf16 paths land about equally far away, and sglang is never further:

| prompt | sglang bf16 vs fp32 (1 / 2 / 4 steps) | Diffusers bf16 vs fp32 (1 / 2 / 4 steps) |
|---|---|---|
| astronaut | 28.0 / 25.5 / 26.7 dB | 28.0 / 25.5 / 26.3 dB |
| fox | 26.2 / 27.1 / 28.8 dB | 26.7 / 25.4 / 25.3 dB |
| library | 28.0 / 25.9 / 26.9 dB | 28.1 / 25.8 / 26.8 dB |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

RTX A6000, 1024×1024, warm requests (ms, three runs; the first is cold):

| steps | sglang | Diffusers |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 12174 (cold), 655, 623 | 4704 (cold), 640, 685 |
| 2 | 695, 698, 741 | 755, 756, 725 |
| 4 | 895, 1004, 840 | 1020, 933, 955 |

Comparable latency. Sprint is not admitted to Breakable CUDA Graph or other fast paths in this PR. `perf_baselines/h100.json` gets entries for both new cases because the server test requires them, but their numbers (0.6B: load ~61 s, e2e ~11.8 s cold, `estimated_full_test_time_s=108.4`; 1.6B: load ~62 s, e2e ~0.39 s, `estimated_full_test_time_s=86.1`) were measured on the A6000, not an H100. They only feed CI sharding while `run_perf_check=False`, so please regenerate them on H100 if you want an accurate shard estimate.

## Test environment

- GPU: 1× NVIDIA RTX A6000 (48 GB, sm_86), driver 610.43.02
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5, 6 vCPU
- Software: Python 3.12.13, torch 2.14.1+cu130, diffusers 0.37.0, transformers 5.19.0, nvcc 13.0.88
- Base: measured on upstream `main` at 363e6c6b4d, then rebased onto 79eb10e182 (the 7 commits in between touch no diffusion code; the Sprint, SANA-Video, registry and harness unit tests re-pass after the rebase)

## Tests run

- `test/unit/test_sana_sprint.py`: 10 passed (14 after the joint commits). They cover the scheduler against Diffusers' Sprint loop, including intermediate-angle and explicit-angle schedules; schedule validation; image-API field forwarding; binning (table, bin choice, latent shape, resize/crop); registry; and the `qk_norm` default. Each case was checked to fail with its targeted change reverted: the bf16 upcast, the `qk_norm` default, the registry priority, binning ignoring its flag, the scheduler ignoring explicit angles, and an undeclared API field.
- `test/unit/test_sana_dit_param_names.py`: 6 passed. This and `test_sana_sprint.py` were re-run on Linux CPU at 527ebc9, after merging main, along with the cfg-warmup and OpenAI image-API unit tests (252 passed).
- Unit tests touching the SANA DiT, SANA-Video stages, registry, OpenAI request helpers, component-accuracy harness, GPU cases or perf baselines: 984 passed.
- `test/server/test_server_1_gpu.py -k sana_sprint`: 2 passed (0.6B and 1.6B). Component accuracy: 3 passed for each of 0.6B and 1.6B.

Not done here:
- **TP/SP.** SANA's DiT has none, and its GLUMBConv feed-forward would need halo exchange to shard spatially. For a 0.6B model running at about 0.7 s per image, it isn't worth it.
- **BCG admission.** I'll do it as a follow-up with the eager-vs-BCG byte-identity and A/B timing evidence that admission requires.
- **CLI flags for the new per-request fields.** The shared sampling parser asks that no model-specific fields be added there. The fields work through the HTTP and Python APIs.
- **Binning for plain SANA.** Diffusers' `SanaPipeline` also bins by default and sglang's SANA does not. That would change existing SANA outputs, so it is left out of this PR.

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Remove per-step host syncs and uploads in image models
issues.body:
Depends on #46045 (host-sync guards in `test/unit/host_sync_guard.py`); this branch is stacked on it.

## Motivation

Several image pipelines read device values on the host or upload constants with pageable copies inside the denoising loop, or redo request-constant work in every forward. Each such read blocks the host until the stream drains, so it cannot queue the next step while the GPU runs this one. This PR removes them model by model. All values are unchanged.

## Modifications

- **Qwen-Image** (`dits/qwen_image.py`, `pipeline_configs/qwen_image.py`, `qwen_image21.py`, `vaes/base.py`, `qwen_image_layered.py`):
  - Layered built `additional_t_cond` with a pageable `torch.tensor([0])` per CFG branch. The branches got different objects, so the DiT's modulation cache never hit on the negative branch and every step recomputed 60 blocks x 2 modulation GEMMs. Both branches now share one device tensor.
  - Batched prompts of different lengths rebuilt their varlen metadata every forward, uploading the lengths from pageable memory (a sync per step and branch). The metadata is cached by its lengths; each forward gets a fresh dict, since attention may memoize into it.
  - Layered's condition-image encode, the channel-wise VAE stats helper (Qwen-Image edit encode/decode, Krea-2, JoyImage) and Qwen-Image-2.1 decode uploaded latent mean/std per request; they are uploaded once per (device, dtype).
- **FLUX.3 Action** (`flux3_action.py`): `cosmos_unipc` called `float(tick)` on each device tick, a sync per step. The ticks are copied to the host once per request; each step still gets the same device tick.
- **Ideogram-4** (`dits/ideogram.py`, `model_specific_stages/ideogram.py`, `progressive_resolution/ideogram.py`): every forward cast the (B, T+I, 53248) fp32 LLM features to bf16, masked them and ran the RMSNorm and the 53248 -> 4608 projection (plus its TP all-gather) on inputs that never change within a request. The stage projects each branch's conditioning on its first step, inside that step's forward context, and passes it to later steps as `llm_cond`. BCG replays still pass the raw features, which their prompt padder pads; the progressive stage drops the projection when the sequence grows. Decode uploads its latent scale/shift once per (device, dtype).
- **GLM-Image** (`dits/glm_image.py`, `pipeline_configs/glm_image.py`): the eager forward dropped the unconditional branch's prior tokens with `prior_embedding[prior_token_drop] *= 0.0`, two nonzero syncs per forward. It now selects `prior_embedding * 0.0` with `torch.where` (same values, signed zeros included). Decode stats are uploaded once.
- **Krea-2** (`pipeline_configs/krea2.py`): without SP the DiT always got a key mask and ran `bool(mask.all())` every forward. The config decides once per request and passes `mask=None` for unpadded prompts, the maskless path the DiT took before.
- **HunyuanImage-3** (`hunyuan_image3_utils.py`, `hunyuan_image3/ar_stage.py`): per step, a pageable timestep upload, host-built `timestep_embedding` frequencies uploaded on every call (five calls per CFG step), `masked_select` on the request-constant image mask for the scatter and the gather, and per-step condition-timestep uploads on the edit path. Positions, device timesteps and condition timesteps are taken once per request, predictions are gathered by position, and the frequencies are uploaded once per device.
- **SenseNova-U1** (`modeling_neo_chat.py`, `modeling_fm_modules.py`): the CFG-window check compared the device timestep in Python (two syncs per step); the window is computed for the whole schedule with the same fp32 comparisons and read once. The timestep embedder's frequencies are uploaded once per device.
- **SANA** (`dits/sana.py`): every block cast the int64 prompt mask to bool; the forward casts it once.

Tests:
- `test_qwen_image_rope.py`: batched prompts of different lengths build their varlen metadata once, and the second forward matches the first bitwise.
- `test_qwen_image_layered.py`: both CFG branches share `additional_t_cond`; VAE and condition-latent stats are uploaded once.
- `test_qwen_image21.py`, `test_glm_image_dit.py`, `test_ideogram4.py`: decode stats/constants are uploaded once and reused bitwise.
- `test_flux3_action.py`: `cosmos_unipc` with `SyncOnRead` ticks matches the plain run bitwise.
- `test_ideogram4.py`: the LLM projection runs once per branch and every step matches the unprojected forward bitwise; BCG replays get the raw features. `progressive_resolution/test_progressive.py`: a resolution change drops the projection.
- `test_glm_image_dit.py`: the prior-token drop runs under `forbid_host_syncs` and equals the graph path's `masked_fill`.
- `test_krea2_pipeline_config.py`: only ragged prompts carry a key mask.
- `test_hunyuan_image3_denoise_step.py`: timestep frequencies are built once; the image-token scatter/gather runs under `forbid_host_syncs` through the precomputed positions.
- `test_sensenova_u1.py`: timestep frequencies are built once per device.
- `test_sana_dit.py`: the prompt mask is cast once per forward, output unchanged.

The model tests run their tiny DiTs on CUDA when the runner has one (the diffusion unit suite runs on an H100).

No hunk overlaps #45942, #45943, #45944, #45948, #45965, #45966, #45967, #45977, #45978, #45979 or #45987; each of them still applies on top of this branch. #45967 also uploads Qwen-Image-2.1 latent stats once, in the encoding stage; this PR covers decode, a different function.

## Accuracy Tests

2xH200 (1 GPU for Qwen-Image-2.1), eager profiles, two requests per model with different inputs. Decoded pixels are bitwise identical to main:

| model (request) | GPUs | outputs compared | main vs PRs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I 1024x1024, 40 steps | 1 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 edit 1024x1024, 40 steps | 1 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Z-Image-Turbo 1024x1024, 9 steps, TP2 | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| FLUX.3 Klein Base 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Ideogram-4 FP8 1024x1024, 20 steps, TP2 | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2I 1280x720, 35 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2V 1280x720x61, 35 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| HunyuanVideo 848x480x61, 30 steps, Ulysses 2 | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| LTX-2 two-stage 768x512x121, 40 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B 1280x720x33, 40 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| MiniMax-H3 T2VA 1344x768 4 s, 12 steps, Ulysses 2 | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |
| MOVA-360p I2VA 640x352x97, 20 steps, TP2 | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Host syncs inside the denoising stage per step (rank 0, `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("warn")` around the stage, real server requests):

| model (request) | main: per step in the loop / per request | this PR: per step in the loop / per request |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I / edit 1024x1024, 40 steps, 1 GPU | 0 / 1 | 0 / 1 |
| Z-Image-Turbo 1024x1024, 9 steps, TP2 | 0 / 2 | 0 / 2 |
| FLUX.3 Klein Base 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG parallel | 0 / 1 | 0 / 1 |
| Ideogram-4 FP8 1024x1024, 20 steps, TP2 | 0 / 5 | 0 / 5 |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2I 1280x720, 35 steps, CFG parallel | 1 / 42 | 1 / 42 (the CFG-window read #45967 removes) |

Client latency, interleaved A/B (main, PR, PR, main), fresh server per run, median of 5 measured requests per run:

| cell | round | main | this PR (with #46045) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ideogram-4 FP8 1024x1024, 20 steps, TP2 | 1 | 3.671 s | 3.588 s |
| | 2 | 3.676 s | 3.589 s |
| | median | 3.673 s | 3.588 s (-2.3%) |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 edit 1024x1024, 40 steps, 1 GPU | 1 | 5.288 s | 5.294 s |
| | 2 | 5.312 s | 5.296 s |
| | median | 5.300 s | 5.295 s (-0.1%, noise) |

- Ideogram-4: the denoising stage went from 3.38 s to 3.29 s; the gain is the LLM projection (and its TP all-gather) no longer running in each of the 40 forwards (20 steps x 2 CFG branches). Each run's 5 requests spread under 0.5%.
- Qwen-Image-2.1 had no per-step syncs on main, so only the per-request decode-stats upload goes away; the change is within noise.
- The per-step sync removals for GLM-Image, HunyuanImage-3, Krea-2, SenseNova-U1, Qwen-Image-Layered/batched prompts, FLUX.3 Action and SANA were not benchmarked on GPU here; their unit tests cover them.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

issues.title: [Fix] diffusion: Respect ancestor cgroup memory headroom
issues.body:
## Motivation

Diffusion host-memory planning can overcommit pinned memory when a parent cgroup has a larger limit but less remaining headroom than the child. For example, a child using 10GiB of 32GiB under a parent using 60GiB of 64GiB has 4GiB remaining, not 22GiB. Sibling usage counts against the parent.

## Modifications

Select the ancestor with the least `max(0, limit - usage)` rather than the least numeric limit. Apply the existing file-cache exclusion before comparison. Extend the existing budget tests with four v1/v2 cases, including cache-adjusted headroom.

## Accuracy Tests

2026-10-21 refresh: the complete changed host-budget test file now also runs through normal package imports in official SGLang nightly `0.5.23.dev20261020+g55b2aef7ad` (PyTorch 2.14.1): baseline 4 failed / 32 passed, candidate **36 passed**. A fresh paired real-SANA nested-cgroup repeat retains pixel-identical images and zero OOM/OOM-kill events. [Nightly unit and paired model evidence](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/b967070464b4c7b45eb9c8c044862fedf43a3ec6/validation/rtx5090-20261017/round3/README.md).

| Check | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Extended host-budget file | 4 failed / 32 passed | 36 passed |
| Actual delegated cgroup v2 + 512MiB anonymous sibling | Overstates headroom and accepts a 128MiB allowance | Rejects that allowance |
| Real SANA 600M, live nested cgroups, one streamed / 27 resident DiT blocks | Books 41,292,288 persistent pinned bytes | Keeps the streamed block pageable |

Both SANA prompts complete with pixel-identical outputs; both arms have zero OOM/OOM-kill events. Ordinary GPU-resident SANA outputs also match. No production OOM was deliberately induced. The isolated fixture releases its unused allocator/cache pages, then calibrates actual cgroup limits once; the production budget calculation is unchanged apart from this patch.

SANA revision: `28f3af7689de15f3883d5863059a2fca0aa9b829` of `Efficient-Large-Model/Sana_600M_1024px_diffusers`, RTX 5090, TP=1, eager, 512×512, two prompts. **Both model arms use the same AutoencoderDC checkpoint-loading prerequisite whose root fix is already in #44690. That prerequisite is not included in this PR.** The budget unit/live-cgroup probes do not depend on that VAE correction.

[Raw budget probe](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/ca72d5212b33ab079f838144467a870de749e859/validation/rtx5090-20261017/evidence/host-budget-live-cgroup.json), [nested baseline](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/ca72d5212b33ab079f838144467a870de749e859/validation/rtx5090-20261017/evidence/sana-cgroup-baseline.json), [nested candidate](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/ca72d5212b33ab079f838144467a870de749e859/validation/rtx5090-20261017/evidence/sana-cgroup-patched.json), [scripts and raw outputs](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/ca72d5212b33ab079f838144467a870de749e859/validation/rtx5090-20261017/README.md).

Original isolated-unit entry points:

```bash
python test_host_budget_linux.py --baseline
python test_host_budget_linux.py
```

Those original runners select the respective main-source budget module with real Linux dependencies. The additional nightly unit run uses normal imports of the complete installed nightly package. The repeated SANA model run still uses SGLang 0.5.21 diffusion dependencies, the complete main-source budget module, and the same disclosed VAE prerequisite in both arms; it is not a full-nightly diffusion-model test. Upstream CI remains necessary.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speedup is claimed. Respecting the parent budget can intentionally select the existing pageable/staged transfer fallback. The goal is to honor headroom and the existing reserve, not to change inference math. GPU validation retained 400W and a 72°C stop threshold.

Targeted duplicate check: #37917 changes residency quotas, #36727 mapped offload/per-rank sharing, #37811 unified-pool residency, and #44540 HiCache physical ownership. Their inspected diffs do not change this function's binding-ancestor selection. [Pinned heads and search limits](https://github.com/yibol9768-alt/sglang/blob/ca72d5212b33ab079f838144467a870de749e859/validation/rtx5090-20261017/evidence/final-diff-audit.json).

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests and this description. The human contributor reviewed the local changes and validation material before authorizing submission.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit; all applicable hooks passed.
- [x] Add focused regression tests in the existing test file.
- [x] Documentation considered: no new public interface or invocation; behavior and limits documented here.
- [x] Provide relevant accuracy/capacity and speed results below, with their measurement limits.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style guidance.

## Review and Merge Process

Maintainer review and upstream CI are requested through the normal merge-oncall/codeowner process. Local results do not replace upstream CI.

issues.title: [diffusion] Qwen-Image 2.1 VAE decoder fast paths: bit-exact norm/bias fusions by default, channels_last decode under quality=extra-high
issues.body:
Independent of the attention PR; both add entries to `kernels/ops/diffusion/__init__.py`, the kernel README and the fast-paths inventory (adjacent lines, trivial to rebase; the inventory section is numbered 18 assuming the attention PR's 17 lands first).

## Motivation

The Qwen-Image 2.1 VAE decode of a 1024x1024 image takes 186 ms on one SM120 GPU. Its decoder (dims 1152/1152/1152/576/288/144, five up blocks that run three residual blocks at their own resolution and then upsample) spends that time on cuDNN convs, but also on work that is pure data movement: cuDNN's NCHW/NHWC transposes around every conv (25 ms), aten's channel RMSNorm chain (fp32 copy + reduce + four pointwise passes + SiLU), a separate bias-add pass after every conv (46 launches, 10 ms) and nearest-2x upsampling that quadruples the pixels before a 3x3 conv.

This PR removes that overhead in two tiers, following the existing VAE fast-path conventions (`VaeFastPathGate` for quality-gated paths, `BitExactFusionGate` first-sight verification for default-on paths):

- **default (`quality=lossless`)**: bit-exact fusions only; the output PNG is unchanged;
- **`quality=extra-high` / `high`**: the decoder switches to channels_last and uses an NHWC norm kernel with its own reduction order plus fp32-folded upsampler weights; documented as close, not bit-exact.

## Modifications

One commit per optimization (`runtime/models/vaes/qwen_image21_vae_cuda_opt.py`, mounted from `platforms/cuda.py::optimize_vae`; parameter names are preserved so checkpoints load unchanged):

1. `a99db03979` **Lossless fast paths (default on)**: `channel_rmsnorm_finish_silu` JIT kernel keeps aten's fp32 `norm(dim=1)` reduction and fuses the pointwise finish (`max(norm, 1e-12)`, divide, scale, gamma, `+0.0`) with SiLU; `FoldedPadConv2d` folds the symmetric `F.pad` of every causal conv into the conv's own padding, verified per (dtype, shape, stride) signature because cuDNN may pick another algorithm; the fold is only attempted above 2^18 output elements, where a bit-exact first-sight match is decisive (two engines with different accumulation orders agree on all but ~1e-4 of the elements, so on a few thousand elements they can match by chance, as the H100 runner showed at a 4x4 test latent).
2. `a99052507b` **channels_last decode under the quality gate**: the decoder flips to channels_last (parameter memory only; flipping back restores the NCHW kernels exactly), `channel_rmsnorm_silu_nhwc` reduces each pixel's channels in a lane group (1-32 lanes per pixel with 16-byte loads, chosen from C by the Python wrapper so the C=144 last stage stays near bandwidth), and the nearest 2x upsample re-labels the merged-batch view with canonical NHWC strides and uses the bit-exact Triton NHWC gather.
3. `119ab3c768` **Upsampler fold (quality gate)**: each `nearest-2x + conv3x3(p1)` becomes one `ConvTranspose2d(k4, s2, p1)` whose kernel is the fp32 sum of the taps each output phase touches (2.25x fewer MACs, no 4x intermediate). The fold helper moves out of the FLUX.2 module into `vaes/conv_fold.py` so both VAEs share it.
4. `53da9a360c` **Conv bias fusions**: aten adds a conv's bias as a separate pass over the output. Each residual block's second conv now runs without its bias and the new bit-exact `bias_residual_add` JIT kernel applies bias and residual in one pass with aten's per-op bf16 rounding (default on, first-sight verified; channels_last-dense or NCHW-contiguous bf16). Under the quality gate the first conv hands its bias to the NHWC norm kernel, so that pass disappears too.
5. `8d1e569f15` **Upsampler bias into the shortcut add**: the shared Wan Triton kernel `dup_up3d_add` takes an optional per-channel bias (aten rounding), so the upsampler conv runs without its bias pass (default on, first-sight verified).
6. `16cadcebe6` kernel README rows, fast-paths inventory entry, pre-commit formatting (a marker benchmark added here was dropped again later in the series).

Fallbacks: spatial-parallel decode, ROCm, `torch.compile`, unsupported layouts and any first-sight mismatch keep the original module chain.

## Accuracy Tests

- Lossless (default) path, bit-exact: the `channel_rmsnorm_finish_silu` section of `test_norm.py` (14), the `bias_residual_add` section of `test_norm.py` (25, `torch.equal` in both layouts), the `dup_up3d_add` bias case in `test_layout.py`, and the Qwen-Image 2.1 VAE section of `test_model_fast_paths.py` (decode of an optimized tiny decoder with the real latent channel count equals the original bit for bit on a 64x64 latent, where every fold site's first-sight comparison is decisive, and again on a second latent while every gate reports verified; a mismatching kernel disables its gate and the decode stays bit-identical; `state_dict` keys unchanged). End to end the same-seed 1024x1024 PNG keeps `main`'s sha256 (`2781b27ac4b17cb1...`) in every lossless launch.
- `extra-high` path: the `channel_rmsnorm_silu_nhwc` section of `test_norm.py` (within two bf16 ulps of the eager chain, >95% of elements bit-identical, all lane-group specializations, fused bias) and the extra-high case in that section (channels_last decode close to the reference, gate off restores bit-identity). End to end, the extra-high image against the lossless image (RGBA, 1024x1024, seed 42; deterministic: the same sha256 on two GPUs and seven launches):

| channel | PSNR (dB) | global SSIM | max abs diff (/255) | changed pixels |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R | 57.75 | 0.99997 | 8 | 10.3% |
| G | 57.85 | 0.99995 | 11 | 9.7% |
| B | 58.90 | 0.99993 | 8 | 8.2% |
| A | 73.80 | 0.99995 | 1 | 0.3% |
| all | 59.35 | - | 11 | 7.1% |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hardware and workload as in the attention PR: one cc 12.0 (SM120) GPU, 73 GB, 350 W cap, torch 2.13.0+cu132, cuDNN 9.20; `sglang serve --performance-mode speed --attention-backend torch_sdpa`, 1024x1024, 40 steps, bf16. Decode times are the `DecodingStage` under `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1`, mean of 3 requests after a warmup request.

VAE decode, whole series on one GPU, interleaved with `main`:

| quality | decode (ms) | vs `main` | e2e HTTP (s) | output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 186.0 | - | 14.010 | sha256 `2781b27a...` |
| lossless (default) | 159.8 | -14.1% | 13.798 (with the attention PR) | identical to `main` |
| extra-high | 100.4 | -46.0% | 13.743 (with the attention PR) | PSNR 59.4 dB vs lossless |

Per commit (single launches on a second GPU of the same type; its `main` decode is 184.4 ms):

| after commit | lossless decode (ms) | extra-high decode (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 lossless fusions | 163.5 | - |
| 2 channels_last + NHWC norm | 163.6 | 126.4 |
| 3 upsampler fold | - | 112.7 |
| 4 conv bias fusions | 160.2 | 101.1 |
| 5 upsampler bias into shortcut add | 158.3 | 99.1 |

Smoke of this exact branch (rebased on `main` @ `3ed56a341b`, one launch each on a second GPU of the same type, stage-profiling cohort): `main` decode 184.4 ms; this PR 158.0 ms lossless (PNG sha256 identical to `main`) and 98.8 ms extra-high (PSNR 59.35 dB vs lossless, same sha256 as on the other GPU).

Kernel level (`marker.do_bench` on the decoder's production shapes, median us; `cuda` = lossless finish kernel with aten's reduction, `cuda_nhwc` = quality-gated kernel):

| channel RMSNorm + SiLU site | eager | Triton finish (main) | cuda | cuda_nhwc |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (1, 144, 1, 1024, 1024) | 5384 | 2432 | 1881 | 559 |
| (1, 288, 1, 1024, 1024) | 10823 | 4893 | 3811 | 1106 |
| (1, 288, 1, 512, 512) | 2657 | 1175 | 915 | 289 |
| (1, 576, 1, 256, 256) | 1249 | 538 | 421 | 147 |

Other measured pieces: the four upsampler `nearest-2x + conv3x3` sites go from 9754 us to 5529 us as ConvTranspose2d; the separate conv-bias adds go from 46 launches / 10.3 ms to 9 launches / 1.2 ms under extra-high (26 launches / 4.6 ms under lossless, where the first conv's bias cannot enter the aten norm reduction); cuDNN's NCHW/NHWC transposes (119 launches, 24.7 ms) disappear under extra-high. What remains of the extra-high decode (~100 ms) is ~80 ms of cuDNN conv, which `cudnn.benchmark` does not improve on this GPU.

issues.body:
## Motivation

Repeated SANA-Video 2.0 requests with the same negative prompt rerun Gemma, and TI2V sampling builds masks and timesteps across every latent channel and spatial position even though they vary only by frame.

## Modifications

- Reuse the shared conditioning cache for negative prompts, preserving its budget, disable option, and input-based cache keys.
- Keep TI2V masks and model timesteps framewise. Expand timesteps only at the scheduler boundary, preserving its per-token interface and sampling equations.
- Cover repeated and changed negative prompts, disabled caching, and compact timestep storage in the existing tests.

## Accuracy Tests

- The regression tests failed before the change and passed afterward. Focused model, pipeline, and cache tests passed in the existing A800 environment; repository pre-commit checks passed.
- All eight eager A/B video pairs matched exactly, both as MP4 files and decoded RGB frames.
- Applying this patch to the BCG branch in #41501 captured both timestep shapes successfully; T2V and TI2V outputs matched eager exactly, with no capture failures or signature misses. This PR has no dependency on that branch.
- A CUDA sampler comparison at the default latent shape preserved every output element and the conditioned first frame. Frame-timestep storage fell from 11.23 MiB to 100 bytes; the scheduler still receives spatial per-token timesteps.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

A800 80GB, 832×480, 81 frames, 50 steps, guidance 8, seed 42, all components resident, torch.compile disabled. Means of three requests after warmup; end-to-end includes lossless video saving.

issues.title: [diffusion] Name the quality tiers after what they guarantee
issues.body:
## Why

`quality` named its strictest tier `lossless` and the tier above it
`extra-high`, which reads as if the faster tier gives up quality. It does not.
The fusions that tier mounts compute the same function; their rounding is no
further from the exact value than the reference's own rounding is, and the
reference path is only one sample of that rounding — it already moves with the
cuBLAS version, the GPU model and the parallel layout, so a TP2 run can never
be bit-identical to a single-card HF reference anyway. Bit-identical output
describes reproducibility, which is worth keeping as its own tier, not quality.

## What

Tiers are named after what they guarantee, and each level includes the ones
before it:

| tier | guarantee | admits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exact` | bit-identical to the reference path in the same environment | scheduling, placement, data movement, reuse of strictly invariant values |
| `lossless` (default) | the same math and the same operand and accumulator precision; only the place or order of the rounding moves | fusions, other kernels, reassociated reductions, higher intermediate precision |
| `high` | may change what is computed | lower precision, sparsity, reuse across steps |

`extra-high` is kept as an alias of `lossless`. **Two things change for
existing callers.** A request that passed `quality="lossless"` for
bit-identical output has to pass `quality="exact"` now: that name is reused,
not just renamed. And `lossless` is the default, so a deployment that never
set `quality` moves off the bit-exact path onto it. In-repo callers are
updated.

### The mechanisms now match the tiers

`BitExactFusionGate` backs paths that are bit-exact by construction and says so
— that is the `exact` tier's mechanism, and its first-sight check exists to
catch a dispatch that changed underneath it. `QualityGatedFusion` mounts per
request, and every entry in `_QUALITY_FUSION_HANDLERS` now declares the lowest
tier that may mount it, instead of one boolean for "any fusion".

Three of the thirteen do not belong where that boolean put them and move to
`high`:

- **FLUX.2 NVFP4 FC1+SwiGLU+quant** quantizes FC2's input before the reference
  BF16 intermediate exists.
- **Ideogram's BF16-native gate RMSNorm** rounds norm statistics the reference
  (`F.rms_norm`) keeps in fp32.
- **SANA-Video BF16-input linear attention** feeds BF16 to a GEMM the reference
  promotes to FP32.

The other ten keep the reference's math and precision and stay in `lossless`.
No fusion moves into `exact`: the default mounts nothing it did not mount
before.

### One admission template instead of per-case tolerances

`test/quality_tier_admission.py`. A hand-picked `atol` cannot separate the two
cases the tier is about — a reassociated reduction and a kernel that dropped
mantissa bits both land "close". The template scores every implementation
against an fp64 evaluation of the same math and judges the candidate against
the path the model runs today: no more than 1.5x its RMS and max error, and no
systematic sign in the error, since a biased rounding accumulates over layers
and steps where a symmetric one cancels. It also pins NaN/Inf/non-contiguous
behavior and exposes a flip rate for the case where a quantizer or threshold
reads the output.

The static conditions stay a review gate: an accumulation below fp32, a lowered
operand precision or a less stable formulation is approximate by construction
and no tolerance admits it. The end-to-end drift band needs a server run and
stays with the model's consistency suite.

### The two library defaults underneath the tiers

`torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32` and
`allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction` are approximate by the definitions
above, and the runtime never set either, leaving every tier's contract to
whichever PyTorch is installed. Each worker now sets both from
`--allow-cudnn-tf32` / `--allow-bf16-reduced-precision-reduction` and logs what
it runs. They stay process-global because they are: a server mixes tiers across
concurrent batches.

The defaults keep PyTorch's own values. Turning TF32 off moves fp32
convolutions — the VAE decoders that default to `vae_precision="fp32"` — off
tensor cores, so making the strict setting the default would slow `exact` down
to buy a guarantee it does not currently promise. A deployment that wants it
passes both as false.

## Validation (1xB200, FLUX.1-dev 1024x1024, 20 steps, seed 42)

The default tier has to be no slower than it was, so it is checked for being
the *same computation*, interleaved main/PR/main/PR on one box:

| arm | output md5 | ms/step |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `origin/main`, default (`lossless`) | `f1e7e33bd68a9558…` | 72 |
| this PR, default (`exact`) | `f1e7e33bd68a9558…` | 69 |
| `origin/main`, default, repeat | `f1e7e33bd68a9558…` | — |
| this PR, default, repeat | `f1e7e33bd68a9558…` | 69 |

Bit-identical output across the four arms: the default runs the same kernels,
and its denoise stage lands at 1.80–1.84 s either way. The tier system itself
works on the same build — `--quality lossless` mounts the fused linear+GELU and
moves to 66 ms/step with a different md5 at 34.5 dB against the exact output
(rounding-level, as the tier claims), and `--quality extra-high` reproduces the
`lossless` output bit for bit, so the alias resolves.

### Why `lossless` is the default

The default already ran 58 unconditionally-mounted fused kernels; what it
withheld were the 13 request-gated ones. Measured on FLUX.1-dev, 1xB200,
interleaved, same seed:

| | output md5 | steady rate |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| default before (`exact`) | `fb4c78b8…` | 14.39 it/s |
| default after (`lossless`) | `f3bf24b8…` | **14.97 it/s** |
| after, with `--quality exact` | **`fb4c78b8…`** — bit-identical to the old default | 14.38 it/s |
| BCG, default before | `fb4c78b8…` | 18.21 it/s |
| BCG, default after | `f3bf24b8…` | **21.96 it/s** |
| BCG, `--quality exact` | **`fb4c78b8…`** | 13.85 it/s |

The default gets faster on both paths, and `exact` still reproduces the old
default bit for bit, so the strict contract costs a request parameter rather
than being lost.

**Flipping it required closing a silent hole first.** A breakable CUDA graph
bakes in whichever fusions were mounted when it was captured, warmup captures
at the default level, and the capture signature covers only tensors. Once the
default mounts fusions, an `exact` request would unmount them and then replay
the fused graph anyway. The old guard could not catch that: it fired on
"something is mounted", which is exactly what an `exact` request is not. The
BCG runner is now keyed by `(module, level)`, so a level warmup never captured
finds an empty runner and takes the eager fallback the runner already has. The
last row above is that fix under test — without it the md5 there would read
`f3bf24b8…`. Removing the old guard also ends the rule that `quality` and BCG
were mutually exclusive.

**Known cost, deliberately not addressed here:** the 79 server cases that take
the default now compare against goldens recorded on the exact path. The image
thresholds are PSNR 28 / SSIM 0.95 and the measured drift is 34.5 dB, so they
pass, but the regression budget is thinner until the goldens are refreshed.

### The tier assignments, measured

Each fusion's tier above was read off what it does to the numbers. The
admission gate then scored those transformations on **real FLUX.1-dev MLP
activations** captured at the fused GELU site (4096x3072 bf16, max/p99 = 8.1,
so the outlier channels are present), against an fp64 evaluation of the same
math and relative to the path the model runs today:

| classified | transformation | RMS error vs the reference path's | gate |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| `lossless` | fused linear+GELU (cublasLt epilogue) | **0.66x** | pass |
| `lossless` | reassociated fp32 reduction (split-K shape) | 0.98x | pass |
| `lossless` | per-token gated residual (Helios / LingBot) | **1.01x** | pass |
| `high` | bf16-accumulated norm statistics (Ideogram) | ~3.8e4 x | reject |
| `high` | BF16-input attention GEMM (SANA-Video) | ~9.9e3 x | reject |
| `high` | quantized FC2 input (FLUX.2 NVFP4) | ~6.9e5 x | reject |

The GEMM epilogue comes out *more* accurate than the reference chain, which is
what the tier predicts: it rounds once where the reference rounds the GEMM
output and then the GELU output. The gated residual is the case that could not
be settled by reading the code -- it moves one rounding earlier, so the
taxonomy only admits it if it measures that way, and at 1.01x it does.

The two groups separate by three to six orders of magnitude, so none of these
verdicts sits near the 1.5x threshold. `test/unit/test_quality_tier_boundary.py`
keeps them honest in CI on DiT-shaped activations.

### The end-to-end gate: the tier moves the pixels less than the GPU count does

The operator-level numbers above say the rounding is small. Whether that is
*small enough* is the tier's end-to-end question, and the standard for it is
the drift the reference path already shows between two legal environments.
Measured on the same box, FLUX.1-dev, same seed:

| comparison | PSNR |
| --- | --- |
| control: `exact` TP1 vs `exact` TP1 again | bit-identical |
| **the band**: `exact` TP1 vs `exact` **TP2** | **32.5 dB** |
| the tier: `exact` vs `lossless`, TP1 | 34.5 dB |
| the tier: `exact` vs `lossless`, TP2 | 37.3 dB |
| both at once: `exact` TP1 vs `lossless` TP2 | 33.0 dB |

Higher PSNR is a smaller difference, so switching tier (34.5 / 37.3 dB) changes
the image *less* than moving the same tier from one GPU to two (32.5 dB) — and
nobody treats TP2 as a quality setting. The control reruns bit-identically, so
this is not run-to-run noise. The tier's drift is inside the band, which is
what the end-to-end gate asks.

### Running the gates against the real kernels found one bug — in the gate

`assert_special_values_match` rejected the real fused linear+GELU on a NaN
input. The kernel was fine: NaN positions matched and the NaN stayed inside
its own row in both paths. The finite values differed by 3.1e-02 where one
bf16 ulp at that magnitude is 3.8e-01 — ordinary rounding — and the gate was
comparing them with `torch.allclose` defaults (rtol=1e-5), which no bf16 fast
path can meet. It now checks what it is for (NaN positions, signed infinities,
shape, exception type) and leaves magnitude to the operator-level gate. Both
real kernels pass all ten special-value cases after the fix.

Unit tests: the quality, fusion-gating, precision, admission, OpenAI-API and
partitioning tests pass (163), plus the new coverage for the taxonomy, the
alias, per-tier mounting, the admission template and the numerics policy.
