issues.title: [Model] Add Boogu-Image base T2I support
issues.body:
## Motivation Add sglang inference support for **Boogu-Image** ([boogu-project/Boogu-Image](https://github.com/boogu-project/Boogu-Image)). The base model is a 10 B DiT (40 layers = 8 double-stream + 32 single-stream, plus 3 refiner groups), conditioned on Qwen3-VL-8B instruction features, decoded via the FLUX.1-dev `AutoencoderKL`. It ships with a bespoke ascending-time flow-match Euler scheduler that has no direct diffusers equivalent, so this PR wires everything needed to run it end-to-end. Scope of this PR: **base T2I only**. Edit / reference-image, Turbo, and the instruct-reasoner variants are intentionally out of scope and will follow separately. ## Modifications - `runtime/models/dits/boogu_image.py` — DiT: `BooguRMSNormZero` / `BooguLayerNormContinuous`, double-stream + single-stream blocks, 3-axis 3D RoPE (`text / ref-image / noise`) with per-sample windows via `BooguRopeBundle` (msgspec.Struct). Batch is folded into the token dim before rotary so sglang's Triton kernel receives 2D `[num_tokens, head_dim//2]` cos/sin; padded rows use the identity rotation (`cos=1, sin=0`) to match upstream `position_ids=0` semantics. 4D↔5D squeeze at the `ImagePipelineConfig` boundary since Boogu is image-only. - `runtime/models/schedulers/scheduling_boogu_flow_match.py` — flow-match Euler on an **ascending** time axis (`t: 0 → 1`, `prev = sample + (t_next − t) · v`), fundamentally different from `FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler`. Ports the upstream v1 logistic shift (`mu = lin(seq_len)` with `x1=256, y1=0.5, x2=4096, y2=1.15`) and v2 shift (`t / (m − mt + t)` with `m = sqrt(seq_len)/120`). - `configs/pipeline_configs/boogu_image.py` — `BooguImagePipelineConfig`. Chat template routes empty instruction → `SYSTEM_PROMPT_DROP`, non-empty → `SYSTEM_PROMPT_4_T2I` (upstream `system_prompt_follows_task_type=False`, no images). Postprocess reads `.last_hidden_state` (norm-applied); `BooguTextEncodingStage` overrides `_forward_text_encoder` to call `text_encoder.model(...)` because the outer `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration.forward` returns a causal-LM output without `last_hidden_state`. `BooguQwen3VLArchConfig` mirrors the `PretrainedConfig` defaults (`output_attentions=False` etc.) that the HF Qwen3-VL `config.json` doesn't ship. - `runtime/pipelines/boogu_image_pipeline.py` — `_load_config` remaps the on-disk `mllm` / `processor` slots to `text_encoder` / `tokenizer` (via `component_paths` redirect) and relabels the non-diffusers `transformer_boogu` / `scheduling_flow_match_euler_discrete_time_shifting` module strings so the loader library-string assertions pass (`ModelRegistry.resolve_model_cls` keys on the class name). - `configs/models/vaes/boogu_image.py` — subclass of `StableDiffusion3VAEArchConfig` (the SD3 arch config *is* the diffusers `AutoencoderKL`), with FLUX.1-dev's `scaling_factor=0.3611`, `shift_factor=0.1159`. - `configs/models/dits/boogu_image.py`, `configs/sample/boogu_image.py` — DiT and sampling defaults (50 steps, guidance 4.0, 1024²). - `configs/models/fsdp.py`, `registry.py` — `is_boogu_image_layer` FSDP predicate; register `BooguImagePipelineConfig` / `BooguImageSamplingParams` behind a `"boogu-image"` path detector. - `runtime/pipelines_core/stages/text_encoding.py` — **the only shared-path change in this PR.** `align_negative_batch_dim` was applied to both negative embeddings and negative masks, but its 2-D branch is only valid for embeddings: a 2-D *embedding* is `(seq, dim)` with no batch axis, so it must gain one (`unsqueeze(0).repeat(B, 1, 1)` — the Z-Image single-prompt case the branch was written for), whereas a 2-D *mask* is already `(batch, seq)` and must be broadcast in place. Conflating them turned a `[1, S_neg]` mask into `[B, 1, S_neg]`, so any consumer reducing over the sequence dim gets a list of lists instead of one length per request — for Boogu that is an HTTP 500 out of the RoPE builder for every dynamically-batched request (`TypeError: can only concatenate list (not "int") to list`). At batch 1 the broadcast is a no-op (`target_batch == 1` returns the tensor unchanged), which is why the one-shot `generate` path never surfaced it. The helper now takes a kw-only `batchless_2d` flag; both mask call sites pass `batchless_2d=False`. - `runtime/models/dits/boogu_image.py` — `@torch.compiler.disable` on `BooguRopeEmbedder.forward`, which is what makes `--enable-torch-compile` usable for this model. Dynamo's polyfill calls `cls.__new__(cls, *args)` and msgspec's C-level `__new__` rejects it, so compiling the DiT raised from the RoPE embedder's `BooguRopeBundle` return value. Position ids depend only on sequence lengths and image sizes, never on the latents, and the call is ~0.5 ms, so keeping it out of the graph costs nothing and lets the remaining 40 layers compile. - `test/unit/test_text_encoding_negative_batch.py` — new. A shared `[1, seq]` negative mask stays 2-D when broadcast to a batch (and still reduces to one length per request); a 2-D `(seq, dim)` embedding still gains a batch axis; batch 1 is unchanged. Follows [`no-getattr-defensive`](.claude/rules/no-getattr-defensive.md), [`no-dataclasses`](.claude/rules/no-dataclasses.md) (new containers are `msgspec.Struct`; config classes are grandfathered `@dataclass`), [`general-code-style`](.claude/rules/general-code-style.md). ## Accuracy Tests - Scheduler: bit-identical to upstream across `static-v1` / `dynamic-v1` / `dynamic-v2` / `do_shift=False` × steps ∈ {50, 40, 28}, and `step()` integration over 40 steps (max delta `0.0`). - Weight loading: 942 checkpoint keys → 888 model params, 0 missing / 0 unexpected / 0 shape mismatch. - Single-GPU T2I end-to-end (1024×1024, guidance 4.0, seed 0): output image aligns with the reference `inference_simple.py` prompt (elderly scavenger + trash can + red traffic light + Leica street-photography aesthetic). - Unit tests: `pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_text_encoding_negative_batch.py -q` → **3 passed**. Shared negative-conditioning / CFG paths re-run to confirm no other model regressed (`test_text_encoding_cache.py`, `test_cfg_gating.py`, `test_sampling_params.py`, plus the new file) → **36 passed, 8 subtests passed**. - Server end-to-end: the benchmark below produced 10 images (1 warmup + 3 sequential + 2 concurrent + 4 concurrent) with zero exceptions in the server log, at scheduler-reported batch sizes 1 / 2 / 4. - The `text_encoding.py` fix is shape-only and a no-op at batch 1, so single-request output is unchanged by construction; the batched shapes are locked by the new unit tests. `@torch.compiler.disable` keeps the RoPE builder in eager rather than altering it, so it does not move numerics either. - 50-step parity vs the upstream diffusers reference (same `seed=42`, cyberpunk prompt / gallery row 1): injecting byte-identical initial noise **and** conditioning into both stacks leaves the initial latent bit-identical (max abs diff `0.0`) and the step-1 latent within **0.53%** rel-L2 (cosine `0.99997`) — a single denoise step is numerically equivalent across backends. Over 50 CFG steps at guidance 4.0 this compounds to step-50 latent rel-L2 ≈ 72% and final-image PSNR 12.3 dB / SSIM 0.40 (see the Qualitative Comparison section), i.e. benign last-bit bf16 kernel drift (FlashInfer/fused vs SDPA), not a structural difference. ## Qualitative Comparison (upstream diffusers vs sglang native) Same weights, `seed=42`, 1024×1024, 50 steps, `guidance_scale=4.0`. Images are width-limited to 320px; click any cell to view full 1024×1024. | Prompt | diffusers (upstream) | sglang (native) | |---|---|---| | A futuristic cyberpunk city at night, neon reflections on wet streets | | | | A cute orange tabby kitten sitting in a field of sunflowers, golden hour lighting, photorealistic | | | | A serene Japanese garden with a red maple tree, koi pond and stone lantern in autumn | | | | A steaming bowl of ramen with a soft-boiled egg and chopsticks, close-up food photography | | | | An astronaut riding a horse on Mars, dramatic cinematic lighting | | |
Parity note (same-seed divergence is expected, not a bug) Feeding byte-identical initial noise **and** identical conditioning embeddings into both stacks: step-1 latent rel-L2 = 0.53% (cosine 0.99997), step-50 = 72%, final image PSNR 12.3 dB / SSIM 0.40. A single denoise step is numerically equivalent between the two backends; the divergence is compounding bf16 kernel drift amplified over 50 CFG steps at guidance 4.0 — a different-but-valid sample from the same distribution, not a structural difference.
## Speed Tests and Profiling H20 (95.6 GiB), bf16, `Boogu-Image-0.1-Base` (10.29B DiT, 40 layers), `guidance_scale=4.0`, `seed=42`, fixed prompt set. Sections 1–3 are 1024²/50 steps with the upstream diffusers pipeline as reference (identical weights, sglang on GPU 2, diffusers on GPU 0); section 4 uses vllm-omni's published 512²/28-step config. The native-backend gate was verified on every sglang run (no `diffusers backend` / `Loaded diffusers pipeline` in any log). Shared env: `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`.
Commands sglang one-shot and server. `serve` opens its HTTP port *before* warmup runs (`/health` answers 200 while the GPU is still warming), so readiness is gated on the `fired up and ready to roll` log line: ```bash python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.entrypoints.cli.main generate \ --backend=sglang --model-path $MODEL --prompt "$PROMPT" \ --width 1024 --height 1024 --num-inference-steps 50 --guidance-scale 4.0 \ --seed 42 --save-output --warmup --dit-cpu-offload false \ --perf-dump-path outputs/diffusion_benchmarks/$LABEL.json \ [--enable-torch-compile] [--enable-cfg-parallel] python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.entrypoints.cli.main serve \ --model-path $MODEL --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31000 \ --batching-max-size 4 --batching-delay-ms 100 \ --enable-batching-metrics --dit-cpu-offload false curl -x '' -s http://127.0.0.1:31000/v1/images/generations \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"prompt":"'"$PROMPT"'","width":1024,"height":1024, "num_inference_steps":50,"guidance_scale":4.0,"seed":42,"n":1}' ``` Upstream diffusers reference. `device=cuda:0` must be exported *before* importing `boogu` — it gates upstream's own fused RMSNorm and fused SwiGLU, so leaving it unset understates the reference. One 50-step warmup pass is discarded: ```python import os; os.environ["device"] = "cuda:0" # before the boogu import import torch from boogu.pipelines.boogu.pipeline_boogu import BooguImagePipeline pipe = BooguImagePipeline.from_pretrained(MODEL, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, trust_remote_code=True).to("cuda:0") # str -> batch 1; list -> batch_size = len(list) (pipeline_boogu.py:2743) pipe(instruction=PROMPT, negative_instruction="", height=1024, width=1024, max_input_image_pixels=1024 * 1024, max_input_image_side_length=2048, num_inference_steps=50, text_guidance_scale=4.0, generator=torch.Generator("cuda:0").manual_seed(42)) ``` Section 4, sglang side — the in-tree benchmark client, one server lifetime per config. With `--enable-torch-compile` *and* `--batching-max-size > 1` the sweep runs twice and only the second, compile-warm pass is reported; see the section 4 caveats for why `--warmup-requests` cannot cover it: ```bash python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.entrypoints.cli.main serve \ --model-path $MODEL --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31011 \ --batching-max-size {1,4} --batching-delay-ms 100 \ --enable-batching-metrics --dit-cpu-offload false --enable-torch-compile true for conc in 1 2 4; do python python/sglang/multimodal_gen/benchmarks/bench_serving.py \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31011 --dataset random --task text-to-image \ --width 512 --height 512 --num-inference-steps 28 \ --num-prompts 10 --max-concurrency $conc --warmup-requests 4 \ --disable-tqdm --output-file c$conc.json done ``` vllm-omni side (their own harness and config, model repointed at our local checkpoint, baseline assertion replaced by `skip-performance-assertion`): ```bash python -m pytest tests/dfx/perf/scripts/run_diffusion_benchmark.py \ --test-config-file tests/dfx/perf/tests/test_boogu_image_h20_local.json -s -v ```
### 1. Optimization stack vs upstream diffusers, one-shot latency The diffusers reference is repeated per row so each sglang config is compared to the closest diffusers configuration — 68.65 s eager (its own fused RMSNorm / SwiGLU / FA on) for the non-compile rows, 66.51 s (+ `torch.compile`) for the compile rows. Head-dim padding and CFG parallel have no equivalent there. | config | diffusers (upstream) | sglang (native) | sglang speedup | sglang vs diffusers | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | eager, 1 GPU | 68.65 | 69.49 | 1.00× | 0.99× | | + `--enable-torch-compile` | 66.51 | 59.87 | **1.16×** | **1.11×** | | + head-dim padded to FA bucket, eager | 68.65 | 64.67 | **1.07×** | **1.06×** | | + head-dim padded + `--enable-torch-compile` | 66.51 | **54.54** | **1.27×** | **1.22×** | | + `--enable-cfg-parallel`, 2 GPU | 68.65 | 34.79 | **2.00×** | **1.97×** | | + CFG parallel ×2 + compile | 66.51 | **29.93** | **2.32×** | **2.22×** | - Eager baselines agree within 1.2%, so the ports are at parity before any lever. - `torch.compile` buys diffusers only 3.1% (68.65 → 66.51, fast paths already on) but 1.16× here — and is reachable only via the `@torch.compiler.disable` change in this PR. Compile × CFG-parallel stacks cleanly: 2.01 × 1.16 = 2.33 predicted vs 2.336× measured. - Best single-GPU 54.54 s is **1.22×** diffusers' own best; CFG-parallel ×2 + compile 29.93 s is **2.22×**. - Head-dim padding routes Boogu's head_dim=120 through FlashAttention by zero-padding Q/K/V to 128 (softmax_scale pinned to 1/√120) and slicing back — the trick `sana_wm_components._sana_wm_sdpa` already uses for head_dim=112. Kernel test matches SDPA within bf16 noise (rel-L2 = 3.9 × 10⁻⁵). The two padding rows were re-measured as a four-cell A/B on one commit, the only variable being `_padded_head_dim` (128 vs `self.head_dim`, which makes the selector reject FA at head size 120 and fall back to `torch_sdpa` — confirmed per cell from the `Attention backends for transformer` log line); all four cells reproduce the table within 0.21%. The gain is resolution-dependent: attention is 22.5% of DiT GPU time at 1024²'s 4352 joint tokens but roughly a third of that at 512²'s 1280, since attention FLOPs grow as S² and the linear layers as S, so the same A/B at 512² returns only +0.27% (section 4). ### 2. Server mode with dynamic batching Warmup is `server warmup req (1024x1024, 2/50 steps)` = 6.12 s, then `fired up and ready to roll` — 210 s from launch. Batch sizes are the scheduler's own `Dynamic batch dispatch` metric, not the request count. Compile rows are compile-warm (first request at a new batch dim recompiles: 315 s at batch 2). SDPA eager (= section 1's `eager, 1 GPU`): | concurrency | scheduler dispatch | per-request latency (s) | wall (s) | img/s | vs 1 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | `size=1/4 delay` | 70.48 / 70.00 / 70.77 → median **70.48** | 70.48 | 0.0142 | 1.000× | | 2 | `size=2/4 delay` | 137.01 / 137.01 | 137.02 | 0.0146 | 1.03× | | 4 | `size=4/4 config_cap:4` | 271.18 ×4 | 271.19 | 0.0148 | 1.04× | Padded FA + `--enable-torch-compile` (= section 1's best single-GPU row): | concurrency | scheduler dispatch | per-request latency (s) | wall (s) | img/s | vs 1 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | `size=1/4 delay` | 55.44 / 55.15 / 55.15 → median **55.15** | 55.44 | 0.0181 | 1.000× | | 2 | `size=2/4 delay` | 110.51 / 110.51 | 110.52 | 0.0181 | 1.00× | | 4 | `size=4/4 config_cap:4` | 218.16 ×4 | 218.17 | 0.0183 | 1.01× | Serving overhead is small — 70.48 s through HTTP + ZMQ + scheduler vs 69.49 s one-shot, **+1.4%**. Padded FA + compile is **1.28× / 1.24× / 1.24×** faster per request at concurrency 1 / 2 / 4, matching section 1's 1.27×. ### 3. Batching headroom at this resolution, vs diffusers | batch | diffusers ms/forward | diffusers img/s | vs 1 | sglang (SDPA) img/s | vs 1 | sglang (padded FA + compile) img/s | vs 1 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 683.3 | 0.0146 | 1.000× | 0.0142 | 1.000× | 0.0181 | 1.000× | | 2 | 1331.9 (1.95×) | 0.0150 | 1.027× | 0.0146 | 1.03× | 0.0181 | 1.00× | | 4 | 2617.5 (3.83×) | 0.0152 | 1.046× | 0.0148 | 1.04× | 0.0183 | 1.01× | diffusers' per-forward scales 1.00 / 1.95 / 3.83 — essentially linear — so one 1024² image (4096 image + 256 instruction = 4352 joint tokens) already saturates the H20 and batching is worth ~1–4% for any implementation. All three curves agreeing on the flat shape is the result: this PR makes batching *correct*, and section 1's multi-GPU path is where throughput comes from. Peak memory, per engine: sglang 29 950 / 34 558 / 44 794 MB (server's own `Peak memory usage`), diffusers 36.91 / 38.54 / 42.54 GiB (`torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated`). ### 4. Cross-engine check against vllm-omni, on the same GPU vllm-omni [PR #4995](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/4995) ports the same model, but on different hardware, so its published numbers support no claim about either implementation. Their stack was installed (own uv venv, `vllm 0.26.0` + vllm-omni at upstream main `67c54777`, torch 2.11.0+cu130) and **their harness and their published config were run on the same H20, GPU 1** — the card our own sweep used. That config is `tests/dfx/perf/tests/test_boogu_image_vllm_omni.json` (512×512, 28 steps, 10 prompts, `max-concurrency` 1/2/4, 4 warmup requests at concurrency 4, negative prompt on, guidance 4.0 with CFG on), **not** the 1024² command in their PR body. Their pipeline profiler costs 0.5–1.0%, so their profiler-off numbers are quoted. 30/30 requests succeeded per run. Medians are used throughout: at 10 prompts / concurrency 4 the run is only 2.5 waves, so the partly-empty first wave biases every mean, while medians match Little's Law within 0.15%. Each engine at its own best. Both harnesses share a client lineage and emit the same fields (`throughput_qps`, `latency_median`), so the rows line up directly: latency is the median of 10 requests at concurrency 1, throughput the best over concurrency 1 / 2 / 4. | engine | best config | per-image latency (s) | throughput (img/s) | |---|---|---:|---:| | vllm-omni | compile on by default; request batching unavailable | 8.502 | 0.1192 | | sglang (this PR) | padded FA + `--enable-torch-compile` | **8.259** | **0.1341** | | ratio (sglang / vllm-omni) | | **1.029×** | **1.125×** | The two sglang figures come from different `--batching-max-size` values — 8.259 s at `maxb 1`, 0.1341 img/s at `maxb 4` — because batching trades 0.115 s of single-image latency (the `--batching-delay-ms 100` window, with nothing to merge at concurrency 1) for +10.7% throughput at concurrency 4. Run `maxb 4` when loaded, `maxb 1` when latency-bound. - **They compile the DiT by default** (`Regional compilation applied to 42 module(s) for repeated blocks [...]`, no flag); our defaults are eager and `batching_max_size = 1` (`server_args.py:355`). Default vs default **we lose 11.6%**, and only this PR unblocks the flip — worth 1.16× here, the same as section 1's 1024² figure. Compile vs compile with batching off the two engines are within 1.6%: the denoising loops are at parity, and the gap above comes from the levers around them. - **Their concurrency curve is flat for a structural reason, not a batching result.** `pipeline_boogu_image.py:201` sets `supports_request_batch = False`; `diffusion_engine.py:205` raises `ValueError` for any `max_num_seqs > 1`; the alternative `--step-execution` path needs `prepare_encode()` / `denoise_step()` / `step_scheduler()` / `post_decode()`, none of which their pipeline implements. Their log confirms `max_num_seqs=1 max_wait_ms=0.0`, `batch_size=1`. Per-pipeline gap, not an engine limit: `qwen_image`, `sd3`, `flux`, `ltx2` all set `supports_request_batch = True`. - **Head-dim padding is nearly free at this resolution** — +0.27% against +7.5% / +9.7% at 1024² in section 1. A 1280-token joint sequence spends far less of its time in attention than a 4352-token one. | lever | sglang (this PR) | vllm-omni Boogu | upstream diffusers | |---|---|---|---| | `torch.compile` on the DiT | 1.16× at both resolutions, unblocked here | on by default | 1.03× | | request batching | +10.7% qps at concurrency 4 | unavailable | +4.6% at batch 4 | | CFG parallel, 2 GPU | **2.00×** | unavailable | unavailable | | stacked | **2.32×** | — | — | Caveats: single run per point. For the `maxb 4` figure the sweep was run twice against one server and the second, compile-warm pass reported — with `--enable-torch-compile` the first request at a previously unseen batch dim recompiles inside the measured window, so cold pass 1 at concurrency 2 reads qps 0.0560 with p99 116.4 s against a 15.51 s median. Their harness posts t2i to `/v1/chat/completions` while `bench_serving.py` posts `/v1/images/generations` (each engine's documented path). All four GPUs carried an external tenant at ~80% utilization throughout, applying to both engines equally — the point of measuring on one box. ## Follow-up work (not in this PR) Called out so reviewers know the current boundary; these will land separately: - **Sequence parallelism (Ulysses/SP).** `--ulysses-degree 2` does not yet work for this model — the latent `rearrange` is over 5 dims and the 7 KV heads do not divide by the SP degree, so it needs a `shard_latents_for_sp` override in `base.py` and a fix to the head-count assert at `usp.py:263`. CFG parallelism in section 1 is unaffected and is the multi-GPU path that works today. - **Cache-DiT (step-layer caching, ~1.5–2× lossy).** Boogu is not yet registered in `_CUSTOM_BLOCK_ADAPTER_SPECS`; the adapter carries a single block-list attribute while Boogu has two (`double_stream_layers` = 8, `single_stream_layers` = 32), so registration has to handle both. Gated on a PSNR/SSIM check since it is lossy. - **Warm up serving benchmarks at the real step count.** `bench_serving.py:591` pins warmup requests to `num_inference_steps=1` because the server overrides them anyway (`warmup_request_builder.py:394` → `Req.set_as_warmup`), and issues them serially — so warmup pre-warms neither the real denoise shape nor a batch dim, and under `--enable-torch-compile` with `--batching-max-size > 1` the first request at each new batch dim recompiles inside the measured window. vllm-omni's harness avoids this by warming at `warmup-num-inference-steps=28, warmup-concurrency=4`. Section 4 works around it by reporting the second of two passes; the fix is to let warmup requests carry the benchmark's step count and concurrency. - **I2I / edit and reference-image** (and Turbo / instruct-reasoner), per the scope note in Motivation. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #30752695530](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30752695530) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #30752695446](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30752695446) --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #35293327136](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35293327136) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #35293327111](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35293327111) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #35293327160](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35293327160)

issues.title: [diffusion] Stream an oversized DiT in auto mode instead of OOMing
issues.body:
## Motivation

With no placement flags, `sglang serve --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.1-I2V-14B-480P-Diffusers` runs out of memory on RTX 4090 24 GB, on 1 GPU and on 8. The auto policy streams the text encoder, image encoder and VAE layer by layer, but leaves the DiT on component offload, which moves the whole 30.5 GiB DiT onto the card for the first request.

The DiT is left out because Wan2.1's deployment config enables DiT layerwise offload only in `memory` mode. That is right for the 1.3B models, which fit, and they share the config: every Wan2.1 variant inherits `WanT2V480PConfig`'s, and `WanI2V480PConfig` also serves the 1.3B Fun-InP. So the mode list cannot simply gain `auto`.

## Modifications

- `auto_tune.py`: in `auto` mode, a model that lists `memory` in `dit_layerwise_offload_modes` now streams the DiT when its weights exceed 80% of the free memory on the least-free selected GPU, and logs why:
  ```
  Auto memory policy for WanI2V480PConfig: the DiT needs 30.5 GiB per GPU in bfloat16, more than 80% of the 23.1 GiB free on the least-free selected GPU, so it streams layer by layer (as with --layerwise-offload-components dit).
  ```
  - The size is taken at the precision the loader uses for the DiT (`--dit-precision`, `component_precisions`) and divided by `--tp-size`.
  - Nothing is sized when the GPUs have at least the model's keep-resident threshold free (60 GB for Wan2.1), so datacenter cards pay no cost.
  - The existing gates run first (explicit DiT placement, FSDP, cache-dit, DMD, platform). A DiT that is replaced or quantized by flags (`--transformer-weights-path`, `--quantization`, SVDQuant, or a transformer entry in `component_paths`, `component_weights_paths` or `component_quantizations`) keeps its declared placement, as does one that cannot be sized.
  - Every size check logs its outcome in one line (streams, fits, or could not be sized, with the flags to use), and the older warning that blamed the missing `auto` entry is no longer printed.
- `loader/utils.py`: `dit_parameter_count()` counts a Diffusers transformer's parameters from its safetensors headers, so the decision is made before any weights download:
  - a local directory is read directly, with the same file selection as `_list_safetensors_files`;
  - a repo id is first looked up in the local Hugging Face cache, honouring `--revision` and `--model-subfolder`;
  - only when that cannot size it are the headers read from the Hub, and an unreachable Hub leaves the DiT unsized instead of retrying;
  - nothing is sized under ModelScope, for overlay source repos (not in the Diffusers layout), for single-file checkpoints, or when the checkpoint is stored with non-float dtypes (quantized).

Which models this can affect: those that list only `memory` in `dit_layerwise_offload_modes` (Wan2.1 and Wan2.2-TI2V-5B, Helios, LingBot-Video-MoE, LingBot-World I2V, SANA-WM), and only when their DiT does not fit, where component offload runs out of memory anyway. Not covered, and left for follow-ups that can validate them: DMD-distilled variants (TurboWan, LongLive-2, LingBot-World causal), which stay behind the existing DMD gate, and models that declare no DiT layerwise mode at all.

## Accuracy Tests

Placement only; the model computation is unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8x RTX 4090 24 GB (PCIe, no P2P between GPUs), Wan2.1-I2V-14B-480P, 480x832, 81 frames, 40 steps, BF16 DiT, eager, one request after warmup, no placement flags:

| command | main (`c7be3e9`) | this PR |
|---|---|---:|
| 1 GPU | OOM on the first request | 834.1 s (20.73 s/step), peak 13.0 GiB |
| 8 GPUs, `--enable-cfg-parallel --ulysses-degree 4` | OOM on the first request | 196.5 s (4.81 s/step), peak 12.6 GiB |

For reference, explicit `--layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder,image_encoder,vae` on main: 20.7 s/step on 1 GPU, 4.82 s/step on 8. The branch is on a newer main whose conditioning cache (#40470) serves the benchmark's repeated prompt and image, so its end-to-end times are about 6 s lower on 1 GPU for reasons unrelated to this PR; compare per step.

Sizing on the test box: I2V-14B from the local cache, pinned revision included, under 0.1 s; T2V-14B from the Hub, 14 shards, about 6 s; 1.3B Fun-InP from the Hub about 1 s. `test_server_args.py` and `test_weight_utils.py`: 227 passed.

Related: #41722 (`--use-fsdp-inference true` alone works on small GPUs), #41723 (OOM message and a 24 GB Wan2.1 recipe).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). The 24 GB recipe is in #41723.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

issues.title: [diffusion] move kernel validation into launchers and simplify dispatch
issues.body:
## Motivation

Diffusion model code repeatedly scans tensor ranks, shapes, dtypes, devices and strides through `can_use_*` predicates before calling launchers that need the same information. Flattening tensors before native validation also hides errors such as swapped batch/sequence dimensions with the same element count. After #42240, residual-gate still retains unreachable alternative implementations.

## Modifications

- Remove 18 tensor capability predicates across RoPE, activation, conditioning, normalization and QKV layout. Narrow five selectors to algorithm configuration: dtype, reduction/head width and hardware capability.
- Validate original tensor dimensions in the C++ launchers for Helios RoPE, SANA FP64 RoPE, LTX-2.5 decoder RoPE, GELU+cat and VDN delta factors. Triton launchers own their input validation.
- Let Qwen native QKNorm/RoPE consume packed projection views through its existing stride-aware device implementation. Validate the complex cache rank and vector alignment in C++. Keep the first-use reference comparison independent of the candidate.
- Keep contiguous residual-gate on JIT CUDA and transposed-dense residual-gate on its tuned Triton implementation. Delete unused kernels and catch-all failure caches. Retain numerical gates, request quality, autograd/compile policy and algorithm-specific fallbacks.
- Let Ideogram pass original 4D cos/sin tables into the RoPE launcher; remove its duplicate tensor scan and flattening while retaining unsupported-layout fallback.
- Select CPU/CUDA from the actual input device. A CPU call must not enter a CUDA launcher and permanently disable a process-wide GPU fusion gate; existing Wan tests reproduce the regression before this fix and pass afterward.
- Preserve device arithmetic and launch tuning; Helios additionally instantiates its existing arithmetic for FP32. Document the selection/validation boundary in the diffusion kernel README.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    M[Model call] --> S[Platform / numerical policy / algorithm configuration]
    S --> C[CHANGED: thin JIT wrapper passes original tensors]
    C --> V[CHANGED: C++ host validates tensor relationships]
    S --> T[CHANGED: Triton launcher validates once]
    V --> K[Existing device kernel and launch tuning]
    T --> K
    S --> E[Existing reference implementation]
```

The paired Helios kernel requires matching Q/K heads and full per-token frequency tables, as produced by the attention module. Unsupported direct kernel inputs now raise before launch; the generic eager helper's arbitrary broadcasting is not a paired-kernel contract. TP RMSNorm retains the separate reference path.

This is a broad launcher cleanup, not a deletion of all backend selectors. Quantization formats, channels-last algorithms, numerical/quality policy and non-NVIDIA implementations retain their own selection. The [expanded design, remaining audit items and reproducible evidence](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/tree/bbuf/diffusion-kernel-cleanup-evidence-20261003/v2) describe the boundaries explicitly.

## Accuracy Tests

Cold-L2 benchmark revision: `290c078825`. Baseline: `5916999afbc`. Dedicated B200, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1.

| Validation | Baseline | Benchmarked revision |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full diffusion kernel directory + namespace | 3002 passed, 89 skipped, 4 failed | **3011 passed, 89 skipped, the same 4 failures** |

Both runs pass 40 subtests. The failures are the existing Ernie QKNorm/RoPE gate verification and three split-rounding/full-width NeoX/packed-KV cases in `test_rope.py`, reproduced on baseline in this environment.

- Existing Ideogram, Ernie RoPE/GeGLU and Wan model tests: **11 passed**.
- Ideogram fullgraph compilation and CUDA Graph replay with replacement inputs: passed for both tested shapes, including B=2.
- 84 cold-L2 workloads plus 7 additional model helpers: output bytes, shapes and strides match baseline in every A/B repetition.
- The previous CPU-fix revision `88882677ee` passed the full model-unit CI (3787 passed, 134 skipped, 3 xfailed, 351 subtests). Its local run additionally executes one sparse-attention ragged-tail case that fails with NaN; the same failure reproduces in the unchanged baseline. The final two-file Ideogram change is covered by the tests/benchmarks above, and the [benchmarked-revision full model-unit CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37139995184/job/111252398758) has also passed.

Validation found and fixed two PR regressions: a CPU call disabling Wan's process-wide CUDA fusion gate, and Ideogram performing model-side checks plus the new launcher checks. No input-legality tests were added. Existing numerical, layout, graph, compilation and backend-selection coverage is retained.

[Full cold-L2 report, source manifests, raw samples, profiling evidence and reproduction scripts](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/tree/bbuf/diffusion-kernel-cleanup-evidence-20261003/v3-cold-l2).

This PR was merged as `bc5a055dd7` on 2026-10-04. Its final head was `a42c97419b`, merging main `1e490772e5`. The conflict-resolution regressions passed: **7 overlay tests and 6 CLIP tests**, within **3806 diffusion unit tests and 351 subtests** (134 skips, 3 xfails). Changed-file pre-commit and [lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37192902988) passed. All final-head CUDA JIT logs were audited: **100/100 + 99/99 H100 files, 66/66 B200 files, 6/6 small-GPU files and 66/66 benchmark files**. H200 selected zero tests. Component accuracy, BCG, B200, 5090, all four single-GPU and all three dual-GPU diffusion partitions passed, some after existing retries. The last dual-GPU partition initially failed LTX2.3 ti2v latency in seven attempts. Its [bounded rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37192903261/job/111426610916) then passed **all 10 assigned generation cases on the first attempt**, with the same final-head integration checkout `3eb5e884dd`. LTX2.3 ti2v measured **277.77 ms average / 277.39 ms median denoise**, below the unchanged **300.192 / 291.348 ms** limits, and passed image consistency (minimum CLIP 0.9801, SSIM 0.7801, PSNR 22.0396). The additional IPC recovery test was skipped and provides no coverage. This was ordinary CI; cold-L2 A/B measurements are reported separately. Several AMD/NPU jobs were canceled at merge; canceled jobs are not counted as passes. The [NPU shard rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37192903089/job/111417707245) passed all four assigned cases; all four final-head NPU diffusion shards have now actually passed. Original final-head CUDA diffusion and NPU diffusion shards are now all audited as passed; AMD follow-up validation remains incomplete.

The [same-runner model A/B diagnostic](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37195886518) completed eight alternating samples under PyTorch 2.14.1, with 5x L2 eviction on both GPUs before each request. Main `1e490772e5` failed 3/4 samples; cleanup `a42c97419b` failed 4/4. Median average-denoise timing was **302.832 -> 308.924 ms (+2.01%)** and median E2E **11148.282 -> 11692.407 ms (+4.88%)**. Both variants varied substantially; these data reproduce baseline failures but do not exclude a small cleanup regression or establish the dependency upgrade as the cause. Original assertions and all failures are retained; the diagnostic job correctly failed. Candidate image checks were not reached.

The [focused H100 kernel comparison](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37197396567/job/111422045296) completed all eight ABBAABBA runs on PyTorch 2.14.1/Triton 3.8.0. All **40 BF16 workloads matched output bytes, shapes and strides**. Before **every measured invocation**, it read/wrote 250 MiB (5x L2), excluded from timing. GPU changes ranged **-0.58% to +0.31%**; all 32 default-path eager cases were faster in this measurement. Three optional `quality=high` cases added **0.410-2.212 us** (up to +5.76%). All raw measurements remain in the job log. These results do not replace the model performance and consistency gates.
 The detailed completed results below belong to the previous head `05027d0ab8`, not the final head. The B200 cold-L2 measurements are from `290c078825` on PyTorch 2.13; they have not been rerun on the merged PyTorch 2.14 stack.

CI fixes included in this branch:

- Update bootstrap/prefill sender and CLIP parallel-context fixtures for upstream constructor changes. Targeted runs passed [13 bootstrap tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37175739799), [40 prefill-allocation tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37172500683) and [6 CLIP tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37172498329).
- Compare fused-store FP8 results by representable code distance. The old 15% relative-error approximation rejects adjacent subnormals: H100 returned codes 3 and 4, a **1-ULP / 25%** difference. The test still permits at most one FP8 step and includes this boundary input. [All 14 tests passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37174338666); the kernel is unchanged. A [diagnostic](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37174121022) checked 10,485,760 random elements across 20 seeds, with maximum distance 1 ULP.
- Pin JoyAI-Echo source weights to `4187f9a53c6eff3a76c51e79bd27f70d10f7591b`: upstream removed the monolithic checkpoint, breaking fresh downloads. Initial downloads, cache repair and cache identity respect the pin. [All 6 overlay tests passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37174734623).
- Correct CUDA-only test markers and synthetic NVIDIA performance-policy fixtures on ROCm. Split all 242 AMD unit files exactly once across four existing shards, preserving assertions, retry coverage and the 30-minute step timeout. [All 220 affected tests passed on H100](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37180035574), including all 18 Qwen CUDA tests and all 3 Wan tests without skips.
- Replace the NPU wheel mirror, which returned HTTP 403, with the official Triton Ascend **3.2.2** ARM release through the existing proxy. Version and dependency constraints are unchanged. [All four diffusion shards passed on the earlier `af1c292ebd` candidate](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37177530891).

Completed verification on previous head `05027d0ab8` (October 4, 2026):

- [Lint passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37181100651), as did changed-file pre-commit. No numerical, quality or performance threshold has been increased.
- [CUDA JIT and diffusion jobs all passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37181101074). JIT file totals: H100 **100/100 + 99/99**, B200 **66/66**, benchmark **66/66**, small **6/6**. The green H200 job selects **zero tests** and provides no H200 coverage.
- Diffusion units passed **3797 tests and 351 subtests**, with 134 skips and 3 xfails; the registered bridge passed 4/4 files. Component accuracy, BCG, B200, 5090, all four single-GPU partitions, all three dual-GPU partitions and the coverage check passed (**47/47 single-GPU and 29/29 dual-GPU cases executed**). Some model cases needed the existing retry policy.
- [Qwen cache-dit passed on its first attempt](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37181101074/job/111373836276): step 49 **63.02 ms < 65.11 ms**, average denoise **80.56 ms**, E2E **4316.95 ms**, with an exact reference-image match. That partition retried Hunyuan3D load latency, not Qwen. [LTX-2.5 passed on attempt 4](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37181101074/job/111373836362) at **260.27 ms** average denoise, below the unchanged **314.148 ms** limit. [JoyAI-Echo and its entire partition passed on attempt 3](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37181101074/job/111373836350).
- [AMD](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37181100988): JIT unit **40/40 files** and benchmark **23/23 files** passed. All four single-GPU shards passed **947 + 894 + 722 + 1015 = 3578 unit tests and 351 subtests**, with 115 skips, 3 xfails and 5 deselections. All **242 files** were assigned across **61 + 61 + 60 + 60** files per shard; logs contain test records from 241 distinct files with no overlap. The remaining file is the existing CUDA-only `ltx2_vae_channels_last` exclusion. Their generation tests also passed. The slowest unit shard, including all nine real-pytest performance-failure/retry cases, finished in **24m 36s**, within the unchanged 30-minute timeout. Dual-GPU shard 0 also passed. Dual-GPU shard 1 failed on MiniMax H3's missing ROCm platform branch, a quantization/linear circular import during standalone AR test collection, and gated LTX-2.5 downloads (HTTP 403).
- [All four NPU diffusion shards passed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37181100773) on the same PR merge. One shard initially could not download Wan's pinned reference image; the original URL returned HTTP 200 (1,234,650 bytes), and [the rerun passed all four assigned cases](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37181100773/job/111379951945), including Wan's image-consistency check. No reference image or validation threshold changed. Unrelated SRT failures keep the broader NPU workflow red.

AMD validation is not yet green. Candidate `51c527f781` adds the missing H3 ROCm branch, defers quantization implementation imports until config lookup, and forwards the existing diffusion HF CI credential to the AMD test container. All 11 quantization mappings are unchanged, and changed-file pre-commit passed. Fresh-process import regression tests accompany the fix. [H100 targeted validation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37186081793) passed **134 tests** across five files; the standalone AR file also collected its test successfully (collection only). [The full AMD dual-GPU stage](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37186084061) failed. Shard 0 passed on its first attempt: **13 generation tests and 1 standalone test passed**, with 1 generation and 4 standalone skips. Shard 1 first passed 11 cases, failed two H3 cases because media probing needs the missing `ffprobe`, and timed out starting LTX-2.5's diffusion decoder. Repeated failures exhausted the 180-minute step timeout; standalone AR tests were not reached. H3 denoising and LTX-2.5 weight downloads now work. A follow-up installs `ffmpeg` for diffusion containers; a [separate instrumented diagnosis](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37199681696) is tracing the remaining LTX-2.5 warmup stall. The candidate was not included in the merged PR; fixes are in [Draft PR #42494](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42494). No test or numerical, quality, performance or startup threshold was relaxed. The earlier [credential-enabled CUDA run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37180355847) remains on `1fcc28877c`, which differs only by four subsequently removed modulation dispatch tests. Results from that run are not substituted for the current-head checks above. Workflow secret rules are unchanged.

The [same-H100 Qwen cache-dit diagnostic](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37175345433/job/111356754040) ran A/B/B/A twice, comparing main `5606fb8592` with `715a644848`. Before each request it evicted 250 MiB (5x the reported 50 MiB L2), outside request timing. E2E medians were **4408.09 -> 4342.33 ms (-1.49%)**; average denoise medians were **81.34 -> 80.23 ms (-1.37%)**. No aggregate slowdown reproduced in these eight samples. Step 49 varied from **11.58–67.32 ms on main** and **40.89–66.75 ms on the branch**; both exceeded the unchanged 65.11 ms limit. Three baseline and two candidate pytest runs failed performance checks; the diagnostic's green status only means all measurements completed. All samples, including the unfavorable main outlier, are in the log. This clears L2 before requests, not before every internal kernel, and does not establish a universal performance guarantee.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Before **every measured invocation**, read/write a **632.5 MiB buffer (5x the reported 126.5 MiB L2)**. Input reset and eviction are excluded from timing. Fixed seed, A/B/B/A process order, 10 warmups and 100 measurements per workload. Ordinary CUDA events measure queued GPU work; a separate eager wall-time measurement includes Python/C++ dispatch and synchronization. Empty timing controls and all raw samples are retained.

- **72 kernel/attention-entry cases:** GPU interval changes **-4.62% to +0.46%, geometric mean -0.19%**. No reproducible device-kernel regression observed.
- **12 Qwen/GLM/Ernie/Wan model helpers:** eager changes **-78.25% to +2.08%**, with a maximum increase of **0.82 us**. Packed Qwen projections benefit from the existing native stride-aware implementation.
- **7 additional Ernie/Ideogram/Sensenova helpers:** eager changes **-7.33% to -0.91%**. Ideogram's duplicate-validation regression previously added about 5.6 us; the final implementation no longer reproduces it.

Bare Triton launcher calls now include checks previously paid by their callers: those eager microbenchmarks can add **2–6 us**. Actual model-helper comparisons include both the old caller checks and the new launcher checks. This is not a claim of zero host overhead for every direct API call or of full-model throughput improvement.

External CUDA Graph event timing showed capture-dependent ~2 us shifts on some tiny operations. Same-revision recaptures, ordinary events and Nsight kernel durations were used to investigate; unfavorable raw runs remain in the report. The four small-kernel profiler medians differ by 0–32 ns. Final-head FP16 residual profiles confirm the same CUDA broadcast kernel/grid, with medians 5216→5216 ns and 31648→31680 ns.

The source comparison confirms 36 retained device definitions unchanged (normalizing only Helios' FP32 type assertion); five deleted definitions belong to dead residual-gate alternatives. These measurements cover the listed B200 shapes and helpers, not every architecture/input or multi-GPU/model configuration. Earlier rotating-input benchmarks are archived as historical data: their capped rotation count did not guarantee cold L2 for small cases.

## Checklist

- [x] Changed-file pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Registered GPU regression tests.
- [x] Kernel entry-point documentation.
- [x] Reproducible accuracy/performance evidence with coverage limits.

issues.title: [diffusion] fix: keep residual_gate_add on the JIT CUDA path for cont…
issues.body:
## Motivation

#41305 replaced the shared `residual_gate_add` JIT CUDA operator with Triton kernels, benchmarked on SANA-Video on H200 where it gained 1.6–1.7% E2E. That PR's profiling confirmed the branch executing there is `_rga_transposed`.

The kernel is also shared by Ideogram, Flux-2, Qwen-Image 2.1, ERNIE-Image and LTX-2, which call it on **contiguous** layouts. There the Triton path costs **13–15.6 µs more host time per call**. The cost is flat in tensor size, so it is per-call dispatch overhead, not slower math — negligible when bandwidth-bound, dominant when launch-bound.

LTX-2 is launch-bound: ~800 calls per denoise step at `(1, 384, 4096)` and `(1, 26, 2048)`, from 8 call sites across 48 layers. That adds ~8 ms per step and moved `ltx_2_two_stage_t2v` and `ltx_2_3_two_stage_ti2v_2gpus` from ~1.12× to 1.20–1.23× of their `h100.json` baselines. The `pr_test` limit is 1.20×, so about half of CI runs now cross it.

Found by bisecting 315 commits on 2× H200. Reverting this one file on current main removes the regression entirely.

## Modifications

One file, +9/−4.

1. Take the Triton path only for the transposed-dense layout it was benchmarked on; contiguous layouts go back to the JIT CUDA kernel. The SANA-Video path is untouched.
2. Drop two redundant `can_use_residual_gate_add_cuda` calls — it ran 3× per invocation at ~2.7 µs each (pre-#41305 ran it twice).
3. Call the custom op directly from `residual_gate_add`, which has already run the same predicate. `residual_gate_add_cuda` stays public and keeps validating.

## Accuracy Tests

The CUDA and Triton backends were compared on **37 configurations** (bf16/fp16, six shapes, full / broadcast / per-token gates, plus transposed-dense) and are **bit-identical** on all of them (`torch.equal`). Both already claimed bit-exact rounding, so routing between them by layout cannot change output.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

2× H200, dependencies pinned, sglang commit the only variable.

Host time per call, bf16, at the shapes LTX-2 actually issues (confirmed by counting dispatch branches over a real run):

| shape | gate | #41305 | this PR | pre-#41305 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `(1, 26, 2048)` | broadcast | 36.50 µs | **23.80 µs** | 23.46 µs |
| `(1, 384, 4096)` | broadcast | 39.18 µs | **23.92 µs** | 23.43 µs |
| `(1, 1536, 4096)` | full | 34.43 µs | **19.91 µs** | 19.19 µs |

`ltx_2_two_stage_t2v` avg denoise step, three runs each:

| build | runs | median |
|---|---|---:|
| `544e46c080` (current main) | 164.7 / 162.5 / 161.6 | 162.5 ms |
| **main + this PR** | 158.2 / 158.1 / 157.4 | **158.1 ms** |
| main + whole file reverted | 157.1 / 156.8 / 157.0 | 157.0 ms |
| `fc9e1c8d29` (before #41305) | 156.3 / 157.9 / 154.7 | 156.3 ms |

Recovers 4.4 ms of the 6.2 ms regression. A ~1.1 ms gap to the full revert remains: 672 of 24000 calls (gate same shape as residual) still fall through to the eager path. Can follow up separately.

The microbenchmark covers contiguous layouts only — I did not measure whether Triton also wins there at SANA-Video's sizes. If it does, the dispatch can be widened on the back of a benchmark covering the other models sharing this kernel; `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/diffusion/bench_residual_gate_add.py` already has workloads for most of them.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — no new behaviour; existing kernel tests plus the bit-exactness check above apply
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing change
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

cc @BBuf

issues.body:
## Motivation and changes

Speed up SANA-Video's residual-gate add on H200 using the **KDA-1.5 + Codex CLI + Kimi K3** candidate. Its transposed residual layout makes the original CUDA implementation expensive; the Triton path tiles along the physical stride-1 token dimension and preserves the original multiply-round-add semantics, output strides, guards, custom-op/fake interface and fallback.

**This PR now changes one production file and retains one kernel family: `residual_gate_add`.** The other 39 families from the earlier version have been removed entirely: any family with a measured regression, or without established material end-to-end benefit, stays at the upstream implementation. No per-shape salvage was used. Existing repository tests are unchanged, and the `kernel-design-agents` coauthor is retained.

Baseline: `c842d32b0ab45753178c5f6420662d7812766aca`. Candidate: `76aa0c6c8db3efd275a250a4b9aa07fd13b23a5a`. All results below were freshly measured with this isolated one-file candidate, so the E2E results are attributable to the retained change. The earlier 40-family combined results are not used as evidence for this revision.

## Kernel validation

NVIDIA H200; three independent processes; CUPTI cold-L2 timing. Speedup is baseline latency / candidate latency. Every original frozen case remains included; two additional actual SANA-Video layouts are reported separately. All measured ratios are at least 1; this is a statement about the tested cases, not a guarantee for arbitrary inputs.

| Workloads | Cases | Three geometric-mean speedups | Worst ratio across all repeats |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Original frozen suite | 33 | 1.2702× / 1.2686× / 1.2698× | 1.0017× |
| SANA-Video captured layouts | 2 | 2.5418× / 2.5434× / 2.5416× | 2.5385× |

SANA layout: BF16 `[1, 32760, 2240]`, transposed residual/output, contiguous update, broadcast gate with the two captured storage offsets. Latency is approximately **331 μs → 130 μs**. Captured-layout correctness and changed-input prepared calls pass. **35 existing residual-gate tests pass**, including dtype/layout/offset, compile, graph and fallback coverage.

[Raw kernel results](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/kernel-benchmarks.json) · [Existing tests](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/existing-tests.log) · [KDA provenance](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/provenance.json) · [All 40 inclusion/removal decisions](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/selection.json)

## Isolated end-to-end results

Model: `Efficient-Large-Model/SANA-Video_2B_480p_diffusers`, revision `db5f398b13ca086d09a50ce156c20527773841b1`; one H200; 832×480, 81 frames, 50 steps, guidance 6, seed 42. Prompt: `A curious raccoon walks through a sunlit forest. motion score: 30.` Eager native SGLang backend; fixed settings and pinned checkpoint in both arms.

Each quality runs two independent **A–B–B–A groups**, eight full saved requests total. Each cell compares the mean of two baseline requests with the mean of two candidate requests. Saved E2E includes scheduler wait and output saving; loading and separately captured profiling runs are excluded. Both groups must improve by at least 1.5% to qualify.

| Quality | Saved E2E group 1 | Saved E2E group 2 | Actual before/after |
|---|---|---|---|
| lossless | 38.840 → 38.190 s (**−1.67%**) | 38.810 → 38.155 s (**−1.69%**) | ![Actual before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/lossless/comparison.gif) |
| high | 36.300 → 35.670 s (**−1.74%**) | 36.295 → 35.700 s (**−1.64%**) | ![Actual before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/high/comparison.gif) |

All eight generated videos per quality are **file-byte and decoded-pixel exact**. GIF previews show baseline left and candidate right. Separate profiles confirm the changed `_rga_transposed` device branch executes in the real request.

- **lossless:** [baseline MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/lossless/baseline.mp4), [candidate MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/lossless/candidate.mp4), [eight-run timing](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/lossless/abba.json), [exact-output audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/lossless/media-audit.json), [device dispatch](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/lossless/device-dispatch.json).
- **high:** [baseline MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/high/baseline.mp4), [candidate MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/high/candidate.mp4), [eight-run timing](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/high/abba.json), [exact-output audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/high/media-audit.json), [device dispatch](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/42d1d19e5f876e7b5977fb55d90073230bce1655/diffusion-prs/kda-residual-gate-h200-20260927/models/high/device-dispatch.json).

These claims cover the listed H200 workloads and this exact PR head. No end-to-end gain is claimed for other models. Further model expansion and the previously paused optimization jobs remain paused. issues.title: [Diffusion] Enable lossless SANA-Video eager conv fusions for 12.6% lower latency
issues.body:
## Motivation

SANA-Video's frame-batched GLUMB activations are much larger than Sana's image workload. Its native eager profile is more than 99% GPU busy, with **80 convolution-bias additions taking 97.77 ms per complete CFG iteration**, before the separate SiLU and multiply kernels. The existing exact convolution post-processing only runs in BCG contexts.

Reuse those fusions for SANA-Video eager inference. Two native A–B–B–A groups on **one H200** reduce worker E2E by **12.58–12.63%** and client E2E including saved video by **12.54–12.67%**. All lossless output videos remain byte-identical.

## Modifications

- Add an explicit eager opt-in to the shared convolution bias+SiLU and bias+GLU helpers; SANA-Video's GLUMB temporal block opts in. The Sana image default-stream policy stays intact.
- Reuse the existing BF16 rounding boundaries, first-sight exactness checks and permanent fallback on mismatch. Gradient-enabled default-stream calls and compiled/non-CUDA paths keep Torch.
- Keep this dispatch-only change focused on the existing helpers; standalone test and benchmark files are omitted. No new CUDA/Triton arithmetic, LayerNorm policy, approximate attention, sampling or checkpoint change.
- Update the existing SANA-Video fusion-coverage row for eager convolution post-processing.

The implementation reuses #34928 and the SANA-Video wiring in #35961. The image-specific CPU-launch regression discussed in #34015 motivates retaining the original default for image callers. This video profile has a different cost distribution. [Source review and execution flow](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/source-review.md).

## Benchmark

`Efficient-Large-Model/SANA-Video_2B_480p_diffusers@db5f398b13ca086d09a50ce156c20527773841b1`, **1× H200**, TP1, native backend, GPU-resident components, BF16 DiT/Gemma2, native FP32 linear-attention accumulation and FP32 latent/VAE policy. Manual performance mode, no torch.compile.

Official video shape: **832×480, 81 frames, 16 fps, 5.0625 s**, 50 requested sampling steps, CFG6, flow shift8, seed42. Fixed 300-token text window and native negative prompt. Prompt: `A curious raccoon walks through a sunlit forest. motion score: 30.` Same-shape warmup at 832×480/81 frames.

Baseline `993d1fccbaafe3e79d91567d2fc1d665cc94fa50`; measured candidate `275113434ffe34412f807514399ba00ef70fa38e`; PR head `64e1e8a92a1942f058b9d6c175f5342198b34709`. Any documentation-only follow-up does not change the measured runtime. Torch2.13.0+cu130, Triton3.7.1, CUDA13.0, driver595.71.05. [Environment](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/environment.json).

Fresh native CLI processes on the same idle GPU; A–B–B–A in each group. The eager comparison is repeated twice. BCG runs use actual capture/replay in both arms and provide a regression comparator. Seconds; parentheses show reduction from each group's arithmetic means:

| Group | Worker E2E | Denoise | Client E2E including MP4 save |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| eager-r1 | 44.7324 → 39.1040 (12.58%) | 41.7766 → 36.1501 (13.47%) | 45.210 → 39.480 (12.67%) |
| eager-r2 | 44.7479 → 39.0949 (12.63%) | 41.7929 → 36.1431 (13.52%) | 45.125 → 39.465 (12.54%) |
| bcg-r1 | 37.7962 → 37.7986 (-0.01%) | 34.8571 → 34.8603 (-0.01%) | 38.175 → 38.175 (0.00%) |

<details><summary>All 12 unprofiled native measurements</summary>

| Group | Arm | Worker E2E | Denoise | Client E2E incl. save | Peak reserved GiB |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| eager-r1 | A1 | 44.6694 | 41.7160 | 45.04 | 20.9199 |
| eager-r1 | B1 | 39.0674 | 36.1122 | 39.45 | 21.0176 |
| eager-r1 | B2 | 39.1406 | 36.1880 | 39.51 | 21.0176 |
| eager-r1 | A2 | 44.7954 | 41.8371 | 45.38 | 20.9199 |
| eager-r2 | A1 | 44.7547 | 41.8005 | 45.14 | 20.9199 |
| eager-r2 | B1 | 39.0982 | 36.1451 | 39.47 | 21.0176 |
| eager-r2 | B2 | 39.0916 | 36.1411 | 39.46 | 21.0176 |
| eager-r2 | A2 | 44.7412 | 41.7853 | 45.11 | 20.9199 |
| bcg-r1 | A1 | 37.7978 | 34.8597 | 38.18 | 23.6758 |
| bcg-r1 | B1 | 37.7905 | 34.8525 | 38.16 | 23.6758 |
| bcg-r1 | B2 | 37.8067 | 34.8682 | 38.19 | 23.6758 |
| bcg-r1 | A2 | 37.7946 | 34.8545 | 38.17 | 23.6758 |

</details>

Worker E2E is perf-dump stage duration before saving, excluding loading/warmup. Client E2E is the native scheduler-request/output-save timer, logged to 0.01 s. Profile and benchmark-export timings are excluded. [All raw perf dumps, configs, source SHAs and logs](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/raw), [complete evidence](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/final-evidence.json).

## Profile and operator benchmark

Each slice contains a complete second positive/negative CFG iteration. CPU third-to-fifth model/graph calls are joined to GPU kernels using CUDA launch correlations. All four slices have zero boundary-crossing GPU kernels. Both BCG profiles contain **eight single-segment graph launches**, with **two in the selected CFG iteration**; no signature miss or eager fallback is accepted.

| Native profile | All kernels | Separate conv post kernels / GPU ms | Fused conv post kernels / GPU ms | Graph launches in slice |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| baseline-eager-profile | 2349 | 200 / 168.9436 | 0 / 0.0000 | 0 |
| baseline-bcg-profile | 2023 | 0 / 0.0000 | 80 / 36.9273 | 2 |
| conv-eager-profile | 2229 | 0 / 0.0000 | 80 / 36.0984 | 0 |
| conv-bcg-profile | 2023 | 0 / 0.0000 | 80 / 36.7944 | 2 |

The fusion removes materialized bias and activation intermediates. Other native operations retain their original implementation. Cumulative device times explain the operators and are not E2E measurements. [Original/sliced traces, source attribution and three-table triage](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/profiles).

Committed-wrapper marker benchmark, rotating inputs, median microseconds. These rows include the **actual convolution and post-processing**, with normal output allocation:

| Operation | Native shape | Eager | Fused |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Pointwise conv + bias + SiLU | [21,2240,30,52] → C13440 | 4459.0695 | 3476.4716 |
| Depthwise conv + bias + GLU | [21,13440,30,52] → C6720 | 3127.3782 | 1174.3818 |

[Raw marker output](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/sana-video-conv-marker.log). Output parity is checked separately against the complete native convolution chain, including temporal convolution.

## Output comparison

The audit covers 26 request records. All **22 valid lossless videos**, including unprofiled and profiled eager/BCG runs, are byte-identical. Independent decoding verifies **81/81 identical frames**, SSIM1, PSNR∞, and no audio stream. The before/after contact sheet was visually inspected.

![Baseline eager, optimized eager and optimized BCG; frames 0,26,53,80](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/output-comparison/comparison.jpg)

[Original baseline MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/baseline.mp4) · [Original optimized eager MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/candidate.mp4) · [Original optimized BCG MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/candidate-bcg.mp4) · [Per-frame hashes](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/output-comparison).

Lossless MP4 SHA256: `bd995912646f473f711d30e452891f7bd61dd594dbc6b4987d6f92bc3210f8a5`.

Separate quality/applicability matrix at the candidate, lossless/high in A–B–B–A order per mode:

| Request | Quality | Applicability | Comparison against lossless |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| quality-bcg-a1 | lossless | valid | exact |
| quality-bcg-a2 | lossless | valid | exact |
| quality-bcg-b1 | high | rejected: cannot be used with breakable cuda graphs | no artifact |
| quality-bcg-b2 | high | rejected: cannot be used with breakable cuda graphs | no artifact |
| quality-eager-a1 | lossless | valid | exact |
| quality-eager-a2 | lossless | valid | exact |
| quality-eager-b1 | high | valid | SSIM mean/min 0.938866/0.923584, PSNR mean/min 31.27/29.93 dB |

[Quality matrix](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2e3f75ee1dc52b396e839442803b6952db7ddcd2/diffusion-prs/sana-video-eager-conv-h200/quality-matrix.json).

## Validation and reproduction

**Validation scope:** The test counts, logs and GPU measurements below are historical results from the recorded benchmark revisions, before test cleanup. The current diff retains the runtime and documentation changes; the dedicated test and benchmark files have been removed. This cleanup does not change runtime code or claim a new GPU measurement.

- **12 tests passed on H200**: five new CUDA tests plus seven existing SANA-Video tests. Coverage includes the full production GLUMB shape, convolution-bias rounding, input preservation, changed-input graph replay, default image policy, mismatch fallback and gradient propagation.
